When the API changes in a way that isn't compatible with older versions, a new version is released.
Each version is identified by its release date, e.g. `2025-04-10`. For more information, please see [Clerk API Versions](https://clerk.com/docs/versioning/available-versions).

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Secret key, obtained under "API Keys" in the Clerk Dashboard.

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-actor-tokens">Actor Tokens</h1>

Allow your users to sign in on behalf of other users.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/authentication/user-impersonation#actor-tokens">External documentation</a>

## Create actor token

<a id="opIdCreateActorToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/actor_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "string",
    "actor": {
      "sub": "user_2OEpKhcCN1Lat9NQ0G6puh7q5Rb"
    },
    "expires_in_seconds": 3600,
    "session_max_duration_in_seconds": 1800
  }'
```

`POST /actor_tokens`

Create an actor token that can be used to impersonate the given user.
The `actor` parameter needs to include at least a "sub" key whose value is the ID of the actor (impersonating) user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_id": "string",
  "actor": {
    "sub": "user_2OEpKhcCN1Lat9NQ0G6puh7q5Rb"
  },
  "expires_in_seconds": 3600,
  "session_max_duration_in_seconds": 1800
}
```

<h3 id="create-actor-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» user_id|body|string|true|The ID of the user being impersonated.|
|» actor|body|object|true|The actor payload. It needs to include a sub property which should contain the ID of the actor.<br>This whole payload will be also included in the JWT session token.|
|» » sub|body|string|true|The ID of the actor.|
|» expires_in_seconds|body|integer|false|Optional parameter to specify the life duration of the actor token in seconds.<br>By default, the duration is 1 hour.|
|» session_max_duration_in_seconds|body|integer|false|The maximum duration that the session which will be created by the generated actor token should last.<br>By default, the duration of a session created via an actor token, lasts 30 minutes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "actor_token",
  "id": "string",
  "status": "pending",
  "user_id": "string",
  "actor": {},
  "token": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "created_at": 0,
  "updated_at": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

> 402 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-actor-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|[ActorToken](#schemaactortoken)|
|400|Bad Request|Request was not successful|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|
|402|Payment Required|Payment required|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|
|403|Forbidden|Feature not enabled|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid request parameters|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-allow-list-block-list">Allow-list / Block-list</h1>

Allow-lists and Block-lists allow you to control who can sign up or sign in
to your application, by restricting access based on the user's email
address or phone number.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/authentication/allowlist">External documentation</a>

## List all identifiers on the allow-list

<a id="opIdListAllowlistIdentifiers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/allowlist_identifiers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /allowlist_identifiers`

Get a list of all identifiers allowed to sign up to an instance

<h3 id="list-all-identifiers-on-the-allow-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|paginated|query|boolean|false|Whether to paginate the results.<br>If true, the results will be paginated.<br>If false, the results will not be paginated.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "object": "allowlist_identifier",
    "id": "string",
    "invitation_id": "string",
    "identifier": "string",
    "identifier_type": "email_address",
    "instance_id": "string",
    "created_at": 0,
    "updated_at": 0
  }
]
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

> 402 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-all-identifiers-on-the-allow-list-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication invalid|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|
|402|Payment Required|Payment required|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|

<h3 id="list-all-identifiers-on-the-allow-list-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

## Add identifier to the allow-list

<a id="opIdCreateAllowlistIdentifier"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/allowlist_identifiers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "identifier": "string",
    "notify": false
  }'
```

`POST /allowlist_identifiers`

Create an identifier allowed to sign up to an instance

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "identifier": "string",
  "notify": false
}
```

<h3 id="add-identifier-to-the-allow-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» identifier|body|string|true|The identifier to be added in the allow-list.<br>This can be an email address, a phone number, or a web3 wallet.|
|» notify|body|boolean|false|This flag denotes whether the given identifier will receive an invitation to join the application.<br>Note that this only works for email address and phone number identifiers.|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-clients">Clients</h1>

The Client object tracks sessions, as well as the state of any sign in and sign up attempts, for a given device.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/references/javascript/client">External documentation</a>

## List all clients

<a id="opIdGetClientList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/clients \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /clients`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns a list of all clients. The clients are returned sorted by creation date,
with the newest clients appearing first.
Warning: the endpoint is being deprecated and will be removed in future versions.

<h3 id="list-all-clients-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|paginated|query|boolean|false|Whether to paginate the results.<br>If true, the results will be paginated.<br>If false, the results will not be paginated.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "object": "client",
    "id": "string",
    "session_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "sessions": [
      {
        "object": "session",
```


`GET /domains`

Use this endpoint to get a list of all domains for an instance.
The response will contain the primary domain for the instance and any satellite domains. Each domain in the response contains information about the URLs where Clerk operates and the required CNAME targets.

## Add a domain

<a id="opIdAddDomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/domains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "is_satellite": true,
    "proxy_url": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /domains`

Add a new domain for your instance.
Useful in the case of multi-domain instances, allows adding satellite domains to an instance.
The new domain must have a `name`. The domain name can contain the port for development instances, like `localhost:3000`.
Set `is_satellite` to `true` to add a satellite domain.
To migrate a production instance from an active provider domain to its first custom primary domain,
set `is_satellite` to `false`. The custom domain becomes active and the provider domain stays attached.
Additional custom primary domains are not supported.
If you're planning to configure the new satellite domain to run behind a proxy, pass the `proxy_url` parameter accordingly.
Adding a custom primary domain returns 403 `domain_managed_by_integration` for applications in a Vercel-managed workspace; change the domain from the Vercel integration instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "is_satellite": true,
  "proxy_url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The new domain name. Can contain the port for development instances.|
|» is_satellite|body|boolean|true|Marks the new domain as satellite. Set to `false` only when migrating a production instance from an active provider domain to a custom domain.|
|» proxy_url|body|string \| null|false|The full URL of the proxy which will forward requests to the Clerk Frontend API for this domain. Applicable only to production instances.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "domain",
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "is_satellite": true,
  "frontend_api_url": "string",
  "accounts_portal_url": "string",
  "proxy_url": "string",
  "development_origin": "string",
  "cname_targets": [
    {
      "host": "string",
      "value": "string",
      "required": true
    }
  ],
  "dns_targets": [
    {
      "host": "string",
      "value": "string",
      "record_type": "CNAME",
      "automation_disposition": "already_satisfied",
      "required": true
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
}
```

## Update a domain

<a id="opIdUpdateDomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/domains/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "proxy_url": "string",
    "is_secondary": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /domains/{domain_id}`

The `proxy_url` can be updated only for production instances.
Update one of the instance's domains. Both primary and satellite domains can be updated.
If you choose to use Clerk via proxy, use this endpoint to specify the `proxy_url`.
Whenever you decide you'd rather switch to DNS setup for Clerk, simply set `proxy_url`
to `null` for the domain. When you update a production instance's primary domain name,
you have to make sure that you've completed all the necessary setup steps for DNS and
emails to work. Expect downtime otherwise. Updating a primary domain's name will also
update the instance's home origin, affecting the default application paths.
Updating the `name` or `is_secondary` of a primary domain returns 403 `domain_managed_by_integration` for applications in a Vercel-managed workspace; change the domain from the Vercel integration instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "proxy_url": "string",
  "is_secondary": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain_id|path|string|true|The ID of the domain that will be updated.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|The new domain name. For development instances, can contain the port,<br>i.e `myhostname:3000`. For production instances, must be a valid FQDN,<br>i.e `mysite.com`. Cannot contain protocol scheme.|
|» proxy_url|body|string \| null|false|The full URL of the proxy that will forward requests to Clerk's Frontend API.<br>Can only be updated for production instances.|
|» is_secondary|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether this is a domain for a secondary app, meaning that any subdomain provided is significant and<br>will be stored as part of the domain. This is useful for supporting multiple apps (one primary and<br>multiple secondaries) on the same root domain (eTLD+1).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "domain",
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "is_satellite": true,
  "frontend_api_url": "string",
  "accounts_portal_url": "string",
  "proxy_url": "string",
  "development_origin": "string",
  "cname_targets": [
    {
      "host": "string",
      "value": "string",
      "required": true
    }
  ],
  "dns_targets": [
    {
      "host": "string",
      "value": "string",
      "record_type": "CNAME",
      "automation_disposition": "already_satisfied",
      "required": true
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
}
```

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-email-addresses">Email Addresses</h1>

A user can be associated with one or more email addresses, which allows them to be contacted via email.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/references/javascript/types/email-address">External documentation</a>

## Create an email address

<a id="opIdCreateEmailAddress"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/email_addresses \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "string",
    "email_address": "string",
    "verified": true,
    "primary": true,
    "notify_primary_email_address_changed": false
  }'
```

`POST /email_addresses`

Create a new email address

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_id": "string",
  "email_address": "string",
  "verified": true,
  "primary": true,
  "notify_primary_email_address_changed": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-email-address-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» user_id|body|string|true|The ID representing the user|
|» email_address|body|string|true|The new email address. Must adhere to the RFC 5322 specification for email address format.|
|» verified|body|boolean \| null|false|When created, the email address will be marked as verified.|
|» primary|body|boolean \| null|false|Create this email address as the primary email address for the user.<br>Default: false, unless it is the first email address.|
|» notify_primary_email_address_changed|body|boolean \| null|false|If set to `true` and the email address is created as the user's new primary,<br>the previous primary email address is notified of the change.<br>By default, no notification is sent.|

## Verify a code sent to an email address

<a id="opIdAttemptEmailAddressVerification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/email_addresses/string/attempt_verification \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "verification_id": "string",
    "code": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /email_addresses/{email_address_id}/attempt_verification`

Checks a one-time code against the verification identified by
verification_id, and returns the verification with its updated status
(`verified`, `unverified`, `expired`, or `failed`) and attempt count, so a
backend driving its own frontend can react on every attempt — an incorrect
or expired code is reported through the status, not as an error. Resubmitting
a verification whose code was already accepted is rejected with a
`verification_already_verified` error. If the code
is correct and the email address is not already verified, it is also marked
as verified as a side effect (just as it would be in a frontend verification
flow); an already verified email address is left unchanged. It never creates
a session; to sign the user in afterwards, mint a sign-in token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "verification_id": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-a-code-sent-to-an-email-address-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email_address_id|path|string|true|The ID of the email address whose code is being verified|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» verification_id|body|string|true|The ID of the verification to check, such as one returned by prepare_verification|
|» code|body|string|true|The verification code that was sent to the email address|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "status": "string",

  "attempts": 0,
  "expire_at": 0,
  "channel": "string"
}
```

## Replace a user's email address

<a id="opIdReplaceUserEmailAddress"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/email_address \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email_address": "string",
    "identification_status": "verified",
    "notify_primary_email_address_changed": false
  }'
```

`PUT /users/{user_id}/email_address`

Replaces all of the user's email addresses with a single primary email address.
By default the new email address is created verified, with the admin verification strategy.
When `identification_status` is `reserved` it is created reserved instead: unverified but usable
for sign-in and locked so no other user can claim it. When it is `unverified` the address is
neither usable for sign-in nor locked. Any existing email addresses are deleted.
If an existing email address is linked to a connected account, the request is rejected; remove
the connected account first.

**Warning:** `identification_status: unverified` can lock the user out of their account. An
unverified email address cannot be used to sign in, so if the user has no other verified or
reserved identifier, deleting their existing email addresses leaves them unable to
authenticate — and unable to verify the new address, since that requires signing in. Recovery
then requires another admin API call.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email_address": "string",
  "identification_status": "verified",
  "notify_primary_email_address_changed": false
}
```

<h3 id="replace-a-users-email-address-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user whose email address to replace|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» email_address|body|string|true|The new email address. Must adhere to the RFC 5322 specification for email address format.|
|» identification_status|body|string|false|Controls the status of the replacement email address. Defaults to `verified`. Set to<br>`reserved` to create it reserved (unverified but usable for sign-in and locked so no<br>other user can claim it), or to `unverified` to create it neither usable for sign-in<br>nor locked.<br><br>**Warning:** `unverified` can lock the user out of their account. An unverified email<br>address cannot be used to sign in, so if the user has no other verified or reserved<br>identifier, they will be unable to authenticate and unable to verify this address.<br>Prefer `reserved` unless you specifically need the address left unclaimed — for<br>example so that another user can also hold it until one of them verifies it.|
|» notify_primary_email_address_changed|body|boolean \| null|false|If set to `true`, the user's previous primary email address is notified that the<br>primary email address has changed. No notification is sent when the replacement<br>is the user's current primary email address. By default, no notification is sent.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» identification_status|verified|
|» identification_status|reserved|
|» identification_status|unverified|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "object": "email_address",
  "email_address": "string",
  "reserved": true,
  "verification": {
    "object": "verification_otp",
    "status": "unverified",
    "strategy": "phone_code",
    "attempts": 0,
    "expire_at": 0,
    "channel": "string",
    "verified_at_client": "string"
  },
  "linked_to": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "id": "string"
    }
  ],
  "matches_sso_connection": true,
  "created_at": 0,
  "updated_at": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json

  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},

}
```

```json
  "subject": "string",
  "markup": "string",
```

## Toggle the delivery by Clerk for a template of a given type and slug

<a id="opIdToggleTemplateDelivery"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/templates/email/string/toggle_delivery \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "delivered_by_clerk": true
  }'
```

`POST /templates/{template_type}/{slug}/toggle_delivery`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Toggles the delivery by Clerk for a template of a given type and slug.
If disabled, Clerk will not deliver the resulting email or SMS.
The app developer will need to listen to the `email.created` or `sms.created` webhooks in order to handle delivery themselves.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "delivered_by_clerk": true
}
```

<a id="opIdUpdateInstance"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/instance \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "test_mode": true,
    "hibp": true,
    "support_email": "string",
    "clerk_js_version": "string",
    "development_origin": "string",
    "allowed_origins": [
      "string"
    ],
    "allowed_subdomains": [
      "string"
    ],
    "subdomain_allowlist_enabled": true,
    "cookieless_dev": true,
    "url_based_session_syncing": true,
    "preferred_sign_in_strategy_when_password_required": "password"
  }'
```

`PATCH /instance`

Updates the settings of an instance

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "test_mode": true,
  "hibp": true,
  "support_email": "string",
  "clerk_js_version": "string",
  "development_origin": "string",
  "allowed_origins": [
    "string"
  ],
  "allowed_subdomains": [
    "string"
  ],
  "subdomain_allowlist_enabled": true,
  "cookieless_dev": true,
  "url_based_session_syncing": true,
  "preferred_sign_in_strategy_when_password_required": "password"
}
```

<h3 id="update-instance-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» test_mode|body|boolean \| null|false|Toggles test mode for this instance, allowing the use of test email addresses and phone numbers.<br>Defaults to true for development instances.|
|» hibp|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the instance should be using the HIBP service to check passwords for breaches|
|» support_email|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» clerk_js_version|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» development_origin|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» allowed_origins|body|[string]|false|For browser-like stacks such as browser extensions, Electron, or Capacitor.js (not officially supported), the instance allowed origins need to be updated with the request origin value. For Chrome extensions popup, background, or service worker pages, the origin is chrome-extension://extension_uuid. For Electron apps using `@clerk/electron`, the origins are the custom renderer scheme registered with `createClerkBridge()`, for example `my-app://renderer`, and, during development, the renderer's dev server origin, for example `http://localhost:5173`. For Capacitor, the origin is capacitor://localhost.<br>Send an empty array to remove all allowed origins. A null value leaves the current list unchanged.|
|» allowed_subdomains|body|[string]|false|Subdomains of the instance's own domains that may originate requests while `subdomain_allowlist_enabled` is true. Each entry is either an exact host (`app.example.com`) or a wildcard anchored on a host beneath one of the instance's domains (`*.preview.example.com`), which covers every host under that anchor but not the anchor itself.<br>Entries are stored folded to lower case with any trailing dot removed, the form the origin check compares against, so entries differing only in those respects are one entry. Entries already stored are not validated again, so a list read back from the instance can always be written again unchanged. Send an empty array to remove all entries. A null value leaves the current list unchanged. Production instances only.|
|» subdomain_allowlist_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether requests from subdomains of the instance's own domains are restricted to `allowed_subdomains`. When false, every subdomain of the instance's domain is accepted. Production instances only.|
|» cookieless_dev|body|boolean \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Whether the instance should operate in cookieless development mode (i.e. without third-party cookies).<br>Deprecated: Please use `url_based_session_syncing` instead.|
|» url_based_session_syncing|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the instance should use URL-based session syncing in development mode (i.e. without third-party cookies).|
|» preferred_sign_in_strategy_when_password_required|body|string \| null|false|When password is required at the instance level, sets the preferred sign-in strategy surfaced to Clerk components. Has no effect when password is not required. Defaults to `password`. Set to an empty string to clear the override.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» preferred_sign_in_strategy_when_password_required|password|
|» preferred_sign_in_strategy_when_password_required|otp|
|» preferred_sign_in_strategy_when_password_required|""|

> Example responses

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

`PATCH /instance/communication`

Replaces the SMS country blocklist for this instance. Pass the full set of ISO 3166-1
alpha-2 country codes that should be blocked; codes that aren't recognized as SMS-tier
countries are silently dropped from the persisted list. Omitting `blocked_country_codes`
is a no-op.

```json
    "string"
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» blocked_country_codes|body|[string]|false|ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to block for SMS delivery. Whole-list replacement. Codes must be uppercase, 2-letter, and unique within the array.|

```json
  "object": "instance_communication",

    "string"
  ]
}
```

```json
    ],
```
```json
    "oauth_jwt_access_tokens": true,

    "pkce_required": true,
    "client_id_metadata_documents_advertised": true,
```

```bash
    "client_id_metadata_documents_block_implicitly_allowed_clients": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /instance/oauth_application_settings`

Updates the OAuth application settings for the instance.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dynamic_oauth_client_registration": true,
  "dynamic_client_allowed_scopes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "default_scopes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "oauth_jwt_access_tokens": true,
  "aud_claim_enabled": true,
  "aud_claim_refresh_backfill_enabled": true,
  "pkce_required": true,
  "client_id_metadata_documents_advertised": true,
  "client_id_metadata_documents_only_allow_pre_registered_clients": true,
  "client_id_metadata_documents_block_implicitly_allowed_clients": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-oauth-application-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» dynamic_oauth_client_registration|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether dynamic OAuth client registration is enabled for the instance (RFC 7591).|
|» dynamic_client_allowed_scopes|body|[string]|false|Administrator-selected scope ceiling for dynamically registered and automatically admitted CIMD clients. Null preserves registered client limits; defaults must be a subset. Fresh user consent is required for expansion.|
|» default_scopes|body|[string]|false|Default scopes assigned when a dynamically registered or first-contact CIMD client omits `scope`. Accepts built-in keys and current custom catalog keys. `advertised` does not affect eligibility. Duplicate keys, unknown keys, and `offline_access` are rejected. An empty array or null resets to Clerk-provided defaults.<br>|
|» oauth_jwt_access_tokens|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether OAuth JWT access tokens are enabled for the instance (disabled indicates opaque access tokens).|
|» aud_claim_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether OAuth access tokens can include an aud claim derived from the RFC 8707 resource parameter.|
|» aud_claim_refresh_backfill_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether refresh grants without a resource can adopt the requested resource when audience claims are enabled.|
|» pkce_required|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether all new OAuth authorization-code requests must use PKCE with the S256 challenge method.|
|» client_id_metadata_documents_advertised|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the instance advertises support for Client ID Metadata Documents in its OAuth authorization server metadata.|
|» client_id_metadata_documents_only_allow_pre_registered_clients|body|boolean \| null|false|When true, new unknown CIMD clients are rejected. Previously auto-connected and pre-registered clients remain admitted; deleting a client makes it unknown again.|
|» client_id_metadata_documents_block_implicitly_allowed_clients|body|boolean \| null|false|When true, recorded implicitly allowed CIMD clients are rejected on future client lookups. Explicitly allowed clients remain accepted. This does not revoke previously issued access tokens.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "oauth_application_settings",
  "dynamic_oauth_client_registration": true,
  "dynamic_client_allowed_scopes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "default_scopes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "oauth_jwt_access_tokens": true,
  "aud_claim_enabled": true,
  "aud_claim_refresh_backfill_enabled": true,
  "pkce_required": true,
  "client_id_metadata_documents_advertised": true,

}
```

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-invitations">Invitations</h1>

Invitations allow you to invite someone to sign up to your application, via email.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/authentication/invitations">External documentation</a>

## List all invitations

<a id="opIdListInvitations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/invitations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /invitations`

Returns all non-revoked invitations for your application, sorted by creation date

<h3 id="list-all-invitations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|query|string|false|Filter invitations based on their status|
|query|query|string|false|Filter invitations based on their `email_address` or `id`|
|order_by|query|string|false|Allows to return invitations in a particular order.<br>At the moment, you can order the returned invitations either by their `created_at`, `email_address` or `expires_at`.<br>In order to specify the direction, you can use the `+/-` symbols prepended in the property to order by.<br>For example, if you want invitations to be returned in descending order according to their `created_at` property, you can use `-created_at`.<br>If you don't use `+` or `-`, then `+` is implied.<br>Defaults to `-created_at`.|
|paginated|query|boolean|false|Whether to paginate the results.<br>If true, the results will be paginated.<br>If false, the results will not be paginated.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

## Create an invitation

<a id="opIdCreateInvitation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/invitations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email_address": "string",
    "public_metadata": {},
    "redirect_url": "string",
    "notify": true,
    "ignore_existing": false,
    "expires_in_days": 1,
    "template_slug": "invitation"
  }'
```

`POST /invitations`

Creates a new invitation for the given email address and sends the invitation email.
Keep in mind that you cannot create an invitation if there is already one for the given email address.
Also, trying to create an invitation for an email address that already exists in your application will result to an error.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email_address": "string",
  "public_metadata": {},
  "redirect_url": "string",
  "notify": true,
  "ignore_existing": false,
  "expires_in_days": 1,
  "template_slug": "invitation"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-invitation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|Required parameters|
|» email_address|body|string|true|The email address the invitation will be sent to|
|» public_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata that will be attached to the newly created invitation.<br>The value of this property should be a well-formed JSON object.<br>Once the user accepts the invitation and signs up, these metadata will end up in the user's public metadata.|
|» redirect_url|body|string|false|Optional URL which specifies where to redirect the user once they click the invitation link.<br>This is only required if you have implemented a [custom flow](https://clerk.com/docs/authentication/invitations#custom-flow) and you're not using Clerk Hosted Pages or Clerk Components.|
|» notify|body|boolean \| null|false|Optional flag which denotes whether an email invitation should be sent to the given email address.<br>Defaults to `true`.|
|» ignore_existing|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether an invitation should be created if there is already an existing invitation for this email address, or it's claimed by another user.|
|» expires_in_days|body|integer \| null|false|The number of days the invitation will be valid for. By default, the invitation expires after 30 days.|
|» template_slug|body|string|false|The slug of the email template to use for the invitation email.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» template_slug|invitation|
|» template_slug|waitlist_invitation|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "invitation",
  "id": "string",
  "email_address": "user@example.com",
  "public_metadata": {},
  "revoked": false,
  "status": "pending",
  "url": "string",
  "expires_at": 0,
  "created_at": 0,
  "updated_at": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|Success|[Invitation](#schemainvitation)|
|400|Bad Request|Request was not successful|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|

## Create multiple invitations

<a id="opIdCreateBulkInvitations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/invitations/bulk \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "email_address": "string",
      "public_metadata": {},
      "redirect_url": "string",
      "notify": true,
      "ignore_existing": false,
      "expires_in_days": 1,
      "template_slug": "invitation"
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /invitations/bulk`

Use this API operation to create multiple invitations for the provided email addresses. You can choose to send the
invitations as emails by setting the `notify` parameter to `true`. There cannot be an existing invitation for any
of the email addresses you provide unless you set `ignore_existing` to `true` for specific email addresses. Please
note that there must be no existing user for any of the email addresses you provide, and this rule cannot be bypassed.

This endpoint is limited to a maximum of 10 invitations per API call. If you need to send more invitations, please make multiple requests.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "email_address": "string",
    "public_metadata": {},
    "redirect_url": "string",
    "notify": true,
    "ignore_existing": false,
    "expires_in_days": 1,
    "template_slug": "invitation"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="create-multiple-invitations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[object]|false|Required parameters|
|» email_address|body|string|true|The email address the invitation will be sent to|
|» public_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata that will be attached to the newly created invitation.<br>The value of this property should be a well-formed JSON object.<br>Once the user accepts the invitation and signs up, these metadata will end up in the user's public metadata.|
|» redirect_url|body|string \| null|false|The URL where the user is redirected upon visiting the invitation link, where they can accept the invitation. Required if you have implemented a [custom flow for handling application invitations](/docs/custom-flows/invitations).|
|» notify|body|boolean \| null|false|Optional flag which denotes whether an email invitation should be sent to the given email address.<br>Defaults to true.|
|» ignore_existing|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether an invitation should be created if there is already an existing invitation for this email<br>address, or it's claimed by another user.|
|» expires_in_days|body|integer \| null|false|The number of days the invitation will be valid for. By default, the invitation expires after 30 days.|
|» template_slug|body|string|false|The slug of the email template to use for the invitation email.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» template_slug|invitation|
|» template_slug|waitlist_invitation|

## Delete an invitation

<a id="opIdDeleteInvitation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/invitations/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /invitations/{invitation_id}`

Permanently deletes the given invitation and the copies of the invitation email Clerk stored for its recipient.
Unlike revoking, deleting removes the invitation record itself, which helps honor a data erasure request from someone who was invited but never signed up.
Other records that contain the same email address, such as users or organization invitations, are not affected.
Invitations of any status can be deleted.

<h3 id="delete-an-invitation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|invitation_id|path|string|true|The ID of the invitation to delete|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "slug": "string",
  "deleted": true,
  "external_id": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

## Revokes an invitation

<a id="opIdRevokeInvitation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/invitations/string/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /invitations/{invitation_id}/revoke`

Revokes the given invitation.
Revoking an invitation will prevent the user from using the invitation link that was sent to them.
However, it doesn't prevent the user from signing up if they follow the sign up flow.
Only active (i.e. non-revoked) invitations can be revoked.

<h3 id="revokes-an-invitation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|invitation_id|path|string|true|The ID of the invitation to be revoked|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-oauth-applications">OAuth Applications</h1>

OAuth applications contain data for clients using Clerk as an OAuth2 identity provider.

## Get a list of OAuth applications for an instance

<a id="opIdListOAuthApplications"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/oauth_applications \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /oauth_applications`

This request returns the list of OAuth applications for an instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The OAuth applications are ordered by descending creation date.
Most recent OAuth applications will be returned first.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-oauth-applications-for-an-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Allows to return OAuth applications in a particular order.<br>At the moment, you can order the returned OAuth applications by their `created_at` and `name`.<br>In order to specify the direction, you can use the `+/-` symbols prepended in the property to order by.<br>For example, if you want OAuth applications to be returned in descending order according to their `created_at` property, you can use `-created_at`.<br>If you don't use `+` or `-`, then `+` is implied. We only support one `order_by` parameter, and if multiple `order_by` parameters are provided, we will only keep the first one. For example,<br>if you pass `order_by=name&order_by=created_at`, we will consider only the first `order_by` parameter, which is `name`. The `created_at` parameter will be ignored in this case.|
|name_query|query|string|false|Returns OAuth applications with names that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>Also returns the OAuth application whose `client_id` is exactly the given query, which is useful for<br>resolving a `client_id` to the OAuth application `id` required by the read, update and delete endpoints.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "oauth_application",
      "id": "string",
      "instance_id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "client_id": "string",
      "client_uri": "string",
      "client_image_url": "string",
      "dynamically_registered": true,
      "consent_screen_enabled": true,
      "pkce_required": true,
      "audience_uri": "string",
      "token_exchange_enabled": true,
      "device_authorization_grant_enabled": true,
      "public": true,
      "scopes": "string",
      "redirect_uris": [
        "string"
      ],
      "callback_url": "string",
      "authorize_url": "string",
      "token_fetch_url": "string",
      "user_info_url": "string",
      "discovery_url": "string",
      "token_introspection_url": "string",
      "created_at": 0,
      "updated_at": 0
    }
  ],
  "total_count": 0
}
```

## Create an OAuth application

<a id="opIdCreateOAuthApplication"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/oauth_applications \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "redirect_uris": [
      "string"
    ],
    "callback_url": "string",
    "scopes": "profile email public_metadata",
    "consent_screen_enabled": true,
    "pkce_required": false,
    "audience_uri": "string",
    "token_exchange_enabled": true,
    "adopt_audience_resource": true,
    "device_authorization_grant_enabled": false,
    "public": true
  }'
```

`POST /oauth_applications`

Creates a new OAuth application with the given name and callback URL for an instance.
The callback URL must be a valid URL.
All URL schemes are allowed such as `http://`, `https://`, `myapp://`, etc...

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "redirect_uris": [
    "string"
  ],
  "callback_url": "string",
  "scopes": "profile email public_metadata",
  "consent_screen_enabled": true,
  "pkce_required": false,
  "audience_uri": "string",
  "token_exchange_enabled": true,
  "adopt_audience_resource": true,
  "device_authorization_grant_enabled": false,
  "public": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-oauth-application-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new OAuth application.<br>Max length: 256|
|» redirect_uris|body|[string]|false|An array of redirect URIs of the new OAuth application|
|» callback_url|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The callback URL of the new OAuth application|
|» scopes|body|string \| null|false|Define the application's built-in and custom scope ceiling. Provide scope keys as a space-delimited string. Custom keys must exist in the instance OAuth scope catalog.|
|» consent_screen_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|True to enable a consent screen to display in the authentication flow.|
|» pkce_required|body|boolean \| null|false|True to require the Proof Key of Code Exchange (PKCE) flow.|
|» audience_uri|body|string \| null|false|An absolute resource URI for a confidential application (RFC 8707 section 2). Registers a resource with no accepted scopes, or adopts an unowned resource with confirmation. Every claimed URI remains permanently reserved to this app, including retirement and deletion, and counts toward the instance resource quota. Changing it stops new exchanges from the old audience immediately. Already-issued tokens retain their lifetime. Clearing requires exchange disabled in an earlier update.|
|» token_exchange_enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable exchanges from the active audience. Requires an audience URI. Disabling preserves target configuration.|
|» adopt_audience_resource|body|boolean|false|Confirm adoption of an existing unowned resource, preserving its accepted scopes and target references. Does not override another application's reservation.|
|» device_authorization_grant_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|True to enable the OAuth Device Authorization Grant for this application. Enabling requires the new OAuth IdP and a reachable device verification page.|
|» public|body|boolean \| null|false|If true, this client is public and you can use the Proof Key of Code Exchange (PKCE) flow.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "oauth_application",
  "id": "string",
  "instance_id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_uri": "string",
  "client_image_url": "string",

    "string"
  ],
  "callback_url": "string",
  "authorize_url": "string",
  "token_fetch_url": "string",
  "user_info_url": "string",
  "discovery_url": "string",
  "token_introspection_url": "string",
  "created_at": 0,
  "updated_at": 0,
  "client_secret": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
      "message": "string",

    }
```

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-oauth-access-tokens">OAuth Access Tokens</h1>

Endpoints for managing OAuth Access Tokens, which are credentials to access protected resources on behalf of a user.

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-organizations">Organizations</h1>

Organizations are used to group members under a common entity and provide shared access to resources.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/organizations/overview">External documentation</a>

## Get a list of organizations for an instance

<a id="opIdListOrganizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations`

This request returns the list of organizations for an instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The organizations are ordered by descending creation date.
Most recent organizations will be returned first.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-organizations-for-an-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_members_count|query|boolean|false|Flag to denote whether the member counts of each organization should be included in the response or not.|
|include_missing_member_with_elevated_permissions|query|boolean|false|Flag to denote whether or not to include a member with elevated permissions who is not currently a member of the organization.|
|query|query|string|false|Returns organizations with ID, name, or slug that match the given query.<br>Uses exact match for organization ID and partial match for name and slug.|
|user_id|query|[string]|false|Returns organizations that include any of the specified user IDs as members. Any user IDs not found are ignored.<br>For each user ID, the `+` and `-` can be prepended to the ID, which denote whether the<br>respective organization should be included or excluded from the result set.|
|organization_id|query|[string]|false|Returns organizations with the organization IDs specified. Any organization IDs not found are ignored.<br>For each organization ID, the `+` and `-` can be prepended to the ID, which denote whether the<br>respective organization should be included or excluded from the result set. Accepts up to 100 organization IDs.<br>Example: ?organization_id=+org_1&organization_id=-org_2|
|order_by|query|string|false|Allows to return organizations in a particular order.<br>At the moment, you can order the returned organizations either by their `name`, `created_at` or `members_count`.<br>In order to specify the direction, you can use the `+/-` symbols prepended in the property to order by.<br>For example, if you want organizations to be returned in descending order according to their `created_at` property, you can use `-created_at`.<br>If you don't use `+` or `-`, then `+` is implied.<br>Defaults to `-created_at`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "organization",
      "id": "string",
```

## Create an organization

<a id="opIdCreateOrganization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "created_by": "string",
    "private_metadata": {},
    "public_metadata": {},
    "slug": "string",
    "max_allowed_memberships": 0,
    "created_at": "string",
    "role_set_key": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /organizations`

Creates a new organization with the given name for an instance.
You can specify an optional slug for the new organization.
If provided, the organization slug can contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters (letters and digits) and the dash "-".
Organization slugs must be unique for the instance.
You can provide additional metadata for the organization and set any custom attribute you want.
Organizations support private and public metadata.
Private metadata can only be accessed from the Backend API.
Public metadata can be accessed from the Backend API, and are read-only from the Frontend API.
The `created_by` user will see this as their [active organization](https://clerk.com/docs/organizations/overview#active-organization)
the next time they create a session, presuming they don't explicitly set a different organization as active before then.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "created_by": "string",
  "private_metadata": {},
  "public_metadata": {},
  "slug": "string",
  "max_allowed_memberships": 0,
  "created_at": "string",
  "role_set_key": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new organization.<br>May not contain URLs or HTML.<br>Max length: 256|
|» created_by|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the User who will become the administrator for the new organization|
|» private_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata saved on the organization, accessible only from the Backend API|
|» public_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata saved on the organization, read-only from the Frontend API and fully accessible (read/write) from the Backend API|
|» slug|body|string \| null|false|A slug for the new organization.<br>Can contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters and the dash "-".<br>Must be unique for the instance.<br>This field should only be included when slugs are enabled in the organization settings, refer to our [documentation](https://clerk.com/docs/guides/organizations/overview#organization-slugs).|
|» max_allowed_memberships|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of memberships allowed for this organization|
|» created_at|body|string \| null|false|A custom date/time denoting _when_ the organization was created, specified in RFC3339 format (e.g. `2012-10-20T07:15:20.902Z`).|
|» role_set_key|body|string \| null|false|The key of the [role set](https://clerk.com/docs/guides/organizations/control-access/role-sets) to assign to this organization.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "organization",
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "slug": "string",
  "image_url": "string",
  "has_image": true,
  "members_count": 0,
  "missing_member_with_elevated_permissions": true,
  "pending_invitations_count": 0,
  "max_allowed_memberships": 0,
  "admin_delete_enabled": true,
  "self_serve_sso_enabled": true,
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {},
  "created_by": "string",

}
```

```json
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

> 402 Response

## Delete an organization

<a id="opIdDeleteOrganization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /organizations/{organization_id}`

Please note that deleting an organization will also delete all memberships and invitations.

<a id="opIdUpdateOrganization"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string \

      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /organizations/{organization_id}`

Updates an existing organization

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {},
  "name": "string",
  "slug": "string",
  "max_allowed_memberships": 0,
  "admin_delete_enabled": true,
  "self_serve_sso_enabled": true,
  "created_at": "string",
  "role_set_key": "string",
  "reassignment_mappings": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization to update|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» public_metadata|body|object \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Metadata saved on the organization, that is visible to both your frontend and backend.<br>Deprecated: As of API version 2026-05-12, this field is rejected on `PATCH /v1/organizations/{organization_id}`. Use `PATCH /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/metadata` to merge updates into existing metadata, or `PUT /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/metadata` to replace a metadata field entirely.|
|» private_metadata|body|object \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Metadata saved on the organization that is only visible to your backend.<br>Deprecated: As of API version 2026-05-12, this field is rejected on `PATCH /v1/organizations/{organization_id}`. Use `PATCH /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/metadata` to merge updates into existing metadata, or `PUT /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/metadata` to replace a metadata field entirely.|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|The new name of the organization.<br>May not contain URLs or HTML.<br>Max length: 256|
|» slug|body|string \| null|false|The new slug of the organization, which needs to be unique in the instance|
|» max_allowed_memberships|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of memberships allowed for this organization|
|» admin_delete_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|If true, an admin can delete this organization with the Frontend API.|
|» self_serve_sso_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether this organization can configure self-serve enterprise SSO.|
|» created_at|body|string \| null|false|A custom date/time denoting _when_ the organization was created, specified in RFC3339 format (e.g. `2012-10-20T07:15:20.902Z`).|
|» role_set_key|body|string \| null|false|The key of the [role set](https://clerk.com/docs/guides/organizations/control-access/role-sets) to assign to this organization.|
|» reassignment_mappings|body|object \| null|false|Maps role keys in the organization's current role set to role keys in the new role set. Only applies when `role_set_key` changes the role set.<br>Every role that a member holds and that the new role set does not include must be mapped, otherwise the request fails with a 422.<br>Mapping a role that both role sets include moves its members to the destination role.<br>Memberships are reassigned asynchronously after the response.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

## Replace metadata for an organization

<a id="opIdReplaceOrganizationMetadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/metadata \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "public_metadata": {},
    "private_metadata": {}
  }'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organization_id}/metadata`

Replace an organization's metadata attributes with the provided values.
Unlike `PATCH /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/metadata` (merge semantics), this
endpoint replaces the supplied metadata fields entirely — the prior contents of each
supplied field are discarded. Fields omitted from the request body are left unchanged.
Prefer the `PATCH` endpoint for partial updates. Use `PUT` only when you explicitly
intend to overwrite a metadata field wholesale.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {}
}
```

<h3 id="replace-metadata-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization whose metadata will be replaced|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» public_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the organization, that is visible to both your frontend and backend.<br>The existing value will be replaced entirely with the new object.|
|» private_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the organization that is only visible to your backend.<br>The existing value will be replaced entirely with the new object.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "organization",
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "slug": "string",
  "image_url": "string",
  "has_image": true,
  "members_count": 0,
```

## Merge and update metadata for an organization

<a id="opIdMergeOrganizationMetadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/metadata \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

    "public_metadata": {},
    "private_metadata": {}
  }'
```

`PATCH /organizations/{organization_id}/metadata`

Update organization metadata attributes by merging existing values with the provided parameters.
Metadata values will be updated via a deep merge.
Deep meaning that any nested JSON objects will be merged as well.
You can remove metadata keys at any level by setting their value to `null`.

```json
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {}
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» public_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the organization, that is visible to both your frontend and backend.<br>The new object will be merged with the existing value.|
|» private_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the organization that is only visible to your backend.<br>The new object will be merged with the existing value.|

## Upload a logo for the organization

<a id="opIdUploadOrganizationLogo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/logo \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'uploader_user_id=string' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organization_id}/logo`

Set or replace an organization's logo, by uploading an image file.
This endpoint uses the `multipart/form-data` request content type and accepts a file of image type.
The file size cannot exceed 10MB.
Only the following file content types are supported: `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`.

```yaml
file: string
```

|body|body|object|false|none|

## Retrieve an organization's billing subscription

<a id="opIdGetOrganizationBillingSubscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/billing/subscription \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id}/billing/subscription`

Retrieves the billing subscription for the specified organization.
This includes subscription details, active plans, billing information, and payment status.
The subscription contains subscription items which represent the individual plans the organization is subscribed to.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-organizations-billing-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization whose subscription to retrieve|

## Retrieve an organization's credit balance

<a id="opIdGetOrganizationBillingCreditBalance"></a>

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id}/billing/credits`

Retrieves the current credit balance for the specified organization.
Credits can be applied during checkout to reduce the charge or automatically applied to upcoming recurring charges.

## Adjust an organization's credit balance

<a id="opIdAdjustOrganizationBillingCreditBalance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/billing/credits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 0,
    "action": "increase",
    "currency": "string",
    "idempotency_key": "string",
    "note": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id}/billing/credits`

Increases or decreases the credit balance for the specified organization.
Each adjustment is recorded as a ledger entry. The idempotency_key parameter
ensures that duplicate requests are safely handled.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "action": "increase",
  "currency": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "note": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="adjust-an-organizations-credit-balance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization whose credit balance to adjust|
|body|body|[AdjustCreditBalanceRequest](#schemaadjustcreditbalancerequest)|true|Parameters for the credit balance adjustment|
|» amount|body|integer(int64)|true|The credit amount in cents. Must be greater than zero.|
|» action|body|string|true|Whether to increase or decrease the credit balance.|
|» currency|body|string|false|The currency code (e.g. "USD"). Defaults to USD if not provided.|
|» idempotency_key|body|string|true|A unique key to ensure the adjustment is applied only once. Repeated requests with the same key return the original ledger entry.|
|» note|body|string|false|An optional note to attach to the ledger entry.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|increase|
|» action|decrease|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-organization-invitations">Organization Invitations</h1>

Invite users to an organization.

## Get a list of organization invitations for the current instance

<a id="opIdListInstanceOrganizationInvitations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organization_invitations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization_invitations`

This request returns the list of organization invitations for the instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
You can filter them by providing the 'status' query parameter, that accepts multiple values.
You can change the order by providing the 'order' query parameter, that accepts multiple values.
You can filter by the invited user email address providing the `query` query parameter.
The organization invitations are ordered by descending creation date by default.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-organization-invitations-for-the-current-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|status|query|string|false|Filter organization invitations based on their status|
|query|query|string|false|Filter organization invitations based on their `email_address`|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

## Create and send an organization invitation

<a id="opIdCreateOrganizationInvitation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/invitations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email_address": "string",
    "inviter_user_id": "string",
    "role": "string",
    "public_metadata": {},
    "private_metadata": {},
    "redirect_url": "string",
    "expires_in_days": 1,
    "notify": true
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id}/invitations`

Creates a new organization invitation and sends an email to the provided `email_address` with a link to accept the invitation and join the organization.
You can specify the `role` for the invited organization member.

New organization invitations get a "pending" status until they are revoked by an organization administrator or accepted by the invitee.

The request body supports passing an optional `redirect_url` parameter.
When the invited user clicks the link to accept the invitation, they will be redirected to the URL provided.
Use this parameter to implement a custom invitation acceptance flow.

You can specify the ID of the user that will send the invitation with the `inviter_user_id` parameter.
That user must be a member with administrator privileges in the organization.
Only "admin" members can create organization invitations.

You can optionally provide public and private metadata for the organization invitation.
The public metadata are visible by both the Frontend and the Backend whereas the private ones only by the Backend.
When the organization invitation is accepted, the metadata will be transferred to the newly created organization membership.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email_address": "string",
  "inviter_user_id": "string",
  "role": "string",
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {},
  "redirect_url": "string",
  "expires_in_days": 1,
  "notify": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-and-send-an-organization-invitation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization for which to send the invitation|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» email_address|body|string|true|The email address of the new member that is going to be invited to the organization|
|» inviter_user_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the user that invites the new member to the organization.<br>Must be an administrator in the organization.|
|» role|body|string|true|The role of the new member in the organization|
|» public_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata saved on the organization invitation, read-only from the Frontend API and fully accessible (read/write) from the Backend API.<br>When the organization invitation is accepted, the metadata will be transferred to the newly created organization membership.|
|» private_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata saved on the organization invitation, fully accessible (read/write) from the Backend API but not visible from the Frontend API.<br>When the organization invitation is accepted, the metadata will be transferred to the newly created organization membership.|
|» redirect_url|body|string \| null|false|Optional URL that the invitee will be redirected to once they accept the invitation by clicking the join link in the invitation email.|
|» expires_in_days|body|integer \| null|false|The number of days the invitation will be valid for. By default, the invitation has a 30 days expire.|
|» notify|body|boolean \| null|false|Optional flag which denotes whether an email invitation should be sent to the given email address.<br>Defaults to `true`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "object": "organization_invitation",
  "id": "string",

  "role": "string",

  },
```

## Bulk create and send organization invitations

<a id="opIdCreateOrganizationInvitationBulk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/invitations/bulk \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

    {
      "email_address": "string",
      "inviter_user_id": "string",

      "private_metadata": {},
      "redirect_url": "string",
      "expires_in_days": 1,
      "notify": true
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id}/invitations/bulk`

Creates new organization invitations in bulk and sends out emails to the provided email addresses with a link to accept the invitation and join the organization.

This endpoint is limited to a maximum of 10 invitations per API call. If you need to send more invitations, please make multiple requests.

You can specify a different `role` for each invited organization member.
New organization invitations get a "pending" status until they are revoked by an organization administrator or accepted by the invitee.
The request body supports passing an optional `redirect_url` parameter for each invitation.
When the invited user clicks the link to accept the invitation, they will be redirected to the provided URL.
Use this parameter to implement a custom invitation acceptance flow.
You can specify the ID of the user that will send the invitation with the `inviter_user_id` parameter. Each invitation
can have a different inviter user.
Inviter users must be members with administrator privileges in the organization.
Only "admin" members can create organization invitations.
You can optionally provide public and private metadata for each organization invitation. The public metadata are visible
by both the Frontend and the Backend, whereas the private metadata are only visible by the Backend.
When the organization invitation is accepted, the metadata will be transferred to the newly created organization membership.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "email_address": "string",
    "inviter_user_id": "string",
    "role": "string",
    "public_metadata": {},
    "private_metadata": {},
    "redirect_url": "string",
    "expires_in_days": 1,
    "notify": true
  }
]
```

|» inviter_user_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the user that invites the new member to the organization.<br>Must be an administrator in the organization.|
|» role|body|string|true|The role of the new member in the organization|
|» public_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata saved on the organization invitation, read-only from the Frontend API and fully accessible (read/write) from the Backend API.<br>When the organization invitation is accepted, the metadata will be transferred to the newly created organization membership.|
|» private_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata saved on the organization invitation, fully accessible (read/write) from the Backend API but not visible from the Frontend API.<br>When the organization invitation is accepted, the metadata will be transferred to the newly created organization membership.|
|» redirect_url|body|string \| null|false|Optional URL that the invitee will be redirected to once they accept the invitation by clicking the join link in the invitation email.|
|» expires_in_days|body|integer \| null|false|The number of days the invitation will be valid for. By default, the invitation has a 30 days expire.|

## Revoke a pending organization invitation

<a id="opIdRevokeOrganizationInvitation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/invitations/string/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "requesting_user_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id}/invitations/{invitation_id}/revoke`

Use this request to revoke a previously issued organization invitation.
Revoking an organization invitation makes it invalid; the invited user will no longer be able to join the organization with the revoked invitation.
Only organization invitations with "pending" status can be revoked.
The request accepts the `requesting_user_id` parameter to specify the user which revokes the invitation.
Only users with "admin" role can revoke invitations.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "requesting_user_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-a-pending-organization-invitation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The organization ID.|
|invitation_id|path|string|true|The organization invitation ID.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» requesting_user_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the user that revokes the invitation.<br>Must be an administrator in the organization.|
