<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-organization-memberships">Organization Memberships</h1>

Manage member roles in an organization.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/organizations/manage-member-roles">External documentation</a>

## Get a list of all members of an organization

<a id="opIdListOrganizationMemberships"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/memberships \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id}/memberships`

Retrieves all user memberships for the given organization

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-all-members-of-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The organization ID.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Sorts organizations memberships by phone_number, email_address, created_at, first_name, last_name or username.<br>By prepending one of those values with + or -, we can choose to sort in ascending (ASC) or descending (DESC) order."|
|user_id|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the user IDs specified. For each user ID, the `+` and `-` can be<br>prepended to the ID, which denote whether the respective user ID should be included or<br>excluded from the result set. Accepts up to 100 user IDs. Any user IDs not found are ignored.|
|email_address|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified email addresses. Accepts up to 100 email addresses. Any email addresses not found are ignored.|
|phone_number|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified phone numbers. Accepts up to 100 phone numbers. Any phone numbers not found are ignored.|
|username|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified usernames.<br>Accepts up to 100 usernames.<br>Any usernames not found are ignored.|
|web3_wallet|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified web3 wallet addresses.<br>Accepts up to 100 web3 wallet addresses.<br>Any web3 wallet addresses not found are ignored.|
|role|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified roles. Accepts up to 100 roles. Any roles not found are ignored.|
|query|query|string|false|Returns users that match the given query.<br>For possible matches, we check the email addresses, phone numbers, usernames, web3 wallets, user IDs, first and last names.<br>The query value doesn't need to match the exact value you are looking for, it is capable of partial matches as well.|
|email_address_query|query|string|false|Returns users with emails that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>For example, `email_address_query=ello` will match a user with the email `HELLO@example.com`.|
|phone_number_query|query|string|false|Returns users with phone numbers that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>For example, `phone_number_query=555` will match a user with the phone number `+1555xxxxxxx`.|
|username_query|query|string|false|Returns users with usernames that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>For example, `username_query=CoolUser` will match a user with the username `SomeCoolUser`.|
|name_query|query|string|false|Returns users with names that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.|
|last_active_at_before|query|integer|false|Returns users whose last session activity was before the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users whose last session activity was before 2023-11-23.|
|last_active_at_after|query|integer|false|Returns users whose last session activity was after the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users whose last session activity was after 2023-11-23.|
|created_at_before|query|integer|false|Returns users who have been created before the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1730160000000 to retrieve users who have been created before 2024-10-29.|
|created_at_after|query|integer|false|Returns users who have been created after the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1730160000000 to retrieve users who have been created after 2024-10-29.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Create a new organization membership

<a id="opIdCreateOrganizationMembership"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/memberships \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "string",
    "role": "string",
    "public_metadata": {},
    "private_metadata": {}
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id}/memberships`

Adds a user as a member to the given organization.
Only users in the same instance as the organization can be added as members.

This organization will be the user's [active organization] (https://clerk.com/docs/organizations/overview#active-organization)
the next time they create a session, presuming they don't explicitly set a
different organization as active before then.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_id": "string",
  "role": "string",
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {}
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-organization-membership-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization where the new membership will be created|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» user_id|body|string|true|The ID of the user that will be added as a member in the organization.<br>The user needs to exist in the same instance as the organization and must not be a member of the given organization already.|
|» role|body|string|true|The role that the new member will have in the organization.|
|» public_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata saved on the organization membership, that is visible to both your frontend and backend.|
|» private_metadata|body|object \| null|false|Metadata saved on the organization membership that is only visible to your backend.|

## Merge and update organization membership metadata

<a id="opIdUpdateOrganizationMembershipMetadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/memberships/string/metadata \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "public_metadata": {},
    "private_metadata": {}
  }'
```

`PATCH /organizations/{organization_id}/memberships/{user_id}/metadata`

Update an organization membership's metadata attributes by merging existing values with the provided parameters.
Metadata values will be updated via a deep merge. Deep means that any nested JSON objects will be merged as well.
You can remove metadata keys at any level by setting their value to `null`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {}
}
```

<h3 id="merge-and-update-organization-membership-metadata-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization to which this membership belongs|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user to which this membership belongs|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» public_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the organization membership, that is visible to both your frontend and backend.<br>The new object will be merged with the existing value.|
|» private_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the organization membership that is only visible to your backend.<br>The new object will be merged with the existing value.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-organization-roles">Organization Roles</h1>

Manage custom roles in an organization.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/organizations/manage-member-roles">External documentation</a>

## Get a list of organization roles

<a id="opIdListOrganizationRoles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organization_roles \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization_roles`

This request returns the list of organization roles for the instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The organization roles are ordered by descending creation date.
Most recent roles will be returned first.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-organization-roles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Returns organization roles with ID, name, or key that match the given query.<br>Uses exact match for organization role ID and partial match for name and key.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Allows to return organization roles in a particular order.<br>At the moment, you can order the returned organization roles by their `created_at`, `name`, or `key`.<br>In order to specify the direction, you can use the `+/-` symbols prepended in the property to order by.<br>For example, if you want organization roles to be returned in descending order according to their `created_at` property, you can use `-created_at`.<br>If you don't use `+` or `-`, then `+` is implied.<br>Defaults to `-created_at`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "role",
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "key": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "is_creator_eligible": true,
      "permissions": [
        {
          "object": "permission",
          "id": "string",
          "name": "string",
          "key": "string",
```

## Create an organization role

<a id="opIdCreateOrganizationRole"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organization_roles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "key": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "permissions": [
      "string"
    ],
    "include_in_initial_role_set": true
  }'
```

`POST /organization_roles`

Creates a new organization role with the given name and permissions for an instance.
The key must be unique for the instance and start with the 'org:' prefix, followed by lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores only.
You can optionally provide a description for the role and specify whether it should be included in the initial role set.
Organization roles support permissions that can be assigned to control access within the organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "key": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "permissions": [
    "string"
  ],
  "include_in_initial_role_set": true
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|

|» key|body|string|true|A unique key for the organization role. Must start with 'org:' and contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Optional description for the role|
|» permissions|body|[string]|false|Array of permission IDs to assign to the role|
|» include_in_initial_role_set|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether this role should be included in the initial role set|

`PATCH /organization_roles/{organization_role_id}`

Updates an existing organization role.
You can update the name, key, description, and permissions of the role.
All parameters are optional - you can update only the fields you want to change.
If the role is used as a creator role or domain default role, updating the key will cascade the update to the organization settings.

> Body parameter

|» key|body|string \| null|false|A unique key for the organization role. Must start with 'org:' and contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores.|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-role-sets">Role Sets</h1>

Role sets define collections of roles that can be assigned to organization members.
Each organization uses one role set to determine the available roles for its members.
Role sets support default roles for new members and creator roles for organization founders.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/organizations/manage-member-roles">External documentation</a>

## Get a list of role sets

<a id="opIdListRoleSets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/role_sets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /role_sets`

Returns a list of role sets for the instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The role sets are ordered by descending creation date by default.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-role-sets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Returns role sets with ID, name, or key that match the given query.<br>Uses exact match for role set ID and partial match for name and key.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Allows to return role sets in a particular order.<br>At the moment, you can order the returned role sets by their `created_at`, `name`, or `key`.<br>In order to specify the direction, you can use the `+/-` symbols prepended in the property to order by.<br>For example, if you want role sets to be returned in descending order according to their `created_at` property, you can use `-created_at`.<br>If you don't use `+` or `-`, then `+` is implied.<br>Defaults to `-created_at`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "role_set",
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "key": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "roles": [
        {
          "object": "role_set_item",
          "id": "string",
          "name": "string",
          "key": "string",
          "description": "string",
          "members_count": 0,
          "has_members": true,
          "created_at": 0,
          "updated_at": 0
        }
      ],
      "default_role": {
        "object": "role_set_item",
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "key": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "members_count": 0,
        "has_members": true,
        "created_at": 0,
        "updated_at": 0
      },
      "creator_role": {
        "object": "role_set_item",
```

## Create a role set

<a id="opIdCreateRoleSet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/role_sets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "key": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "default_role_key": "string",
    "creator_role_key": "string",
    "type": "initial",
    "roles": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /role_sets`

Creates a new role set with the given name and roles.
The key must be unique for the instance and start with the 'role_set:' prefix, followed by lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores only.
You must provide at least one role and specify a default role key and creator role key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "key": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "default_role_key": "string",
  "creator_role_key": "string",
  "type": "initial",
  "roles": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-role-set-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new role set|
|» key|body|string|false|A unique key for the role set. Must start with 'role_set:' and contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores.<br>If not provided, a key will be generated from the name.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Optional description for the role set|
|» default_role_key|body|string|true|The key of the role to use as the default role for new organization members.<br>Must be one of the roles in the `roles` array.|
|» creator_role_key|body|string|true|The key of the role to assign to organization creators.<br>Must be one of the roles in the `roles` array.|
|» type|body|string|false|The type of the role set. "initial" role sets are the default for new organizations.<br>Only one role set can be "initial" per instance.|
|» roles|body|[string]|true|Array of role keys to include in the role set.<br>Must contain at least one role and no more than 10 roles.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|initial|
|» type|custom|

## Update a role set

<a id="opIdUpdateRoleSet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/role_sets/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "key": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "type": "initial",
    "default_role_key": "string",
    "creator_role_key": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /role_sets/{role_set_key_or_id}`

Updates an existing role set.
You can update the name, key, description, type, default role, or creator role.
All parameters are optional - you can update only the fields you want to change.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "key": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "type": "initial",
  "default_role_key": "string",
  "creator_role_key": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-role-set-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role_set_key_or_id|path|string|true|The key or ID of the role set to update|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|The new name for the role set|
|» key|body|string \| null|false|A unique key for the role set. Must start with 'role_set:' and contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Optional description for the role set|
|» type|body|string \| null|false|Set to "initial" to make this the default role set for new organizations.<br>Only one role set can be "initial" per instance; setting this will change any existing initial role set to "custom".|
|» default_role_key|body|string \| null|false|The key of the role to use as the default role for new organization members.<br>Must be an existing role in the role set.|
|» creator_role_key|body|string \| null|false|The key of the role to assign to organization creators.<br>Must be an existing role in the role set.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|initial|

## Replace a role set

<a id="opIdReplaceRoleSet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/role_sets/string/replace \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "dest_role_set_key": "string",
    "reassignment_mappings": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /role_sets/{role_set_key_or_id}/replace`

Replaces a role set with another role set. This is functionally equivalent to deleting
the role set but allows for atomic replacement with migration support.
Organizations using this role set will be migrated to the destination role set.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dest_role_set_key": "string",
  "reassignment_mappings": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="replace-a-role-set-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role_set_key_or_id|path|string|true|The key or ID of the role set to replace|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» dest_role_set_key|body|string|true|The key of the destination role set|
|» reassignment_mappings|body|object|false|Mappings from source role keys to destination role keys.<br>Required if members have roles that need to be reassigned.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

## Add roles to a role set

<a id="opIdAddRolesToRoleSet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/role_sets/string/roles \
```

`POST /role_sets/{role_set_key_or_id}/roles`

Adds one or more roles to an existing role set.
You can optionally update the default role or creator role when adding new roles.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "role_keys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "default_role_key": "string",
  "creator_role_key": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role_set_key_or_id|path|string|true|The key or ID of the role set|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» role_keys|body|[string]|true|Array of role keys to add to the role set.<br>Must contain at least one role and no more than 10 roles.|
|» default_role_key|body|string|false|Optionally update the default role to one of the newly added roles.|
|» creator_role_key|body|string|false|Optionally update the creator role to one of the newly added roles.|

## Replace a role in a role set

<a id="opIdReplaceRoleInRoleSet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/role_sets/string/roles/replace \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "role_key": "string",
    "to_role_key": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /role_sets/{role_set_key_or_id}/roles/replace`

Replaces a role in a role set with another role. This atomically removes
the source role and reassigns any members to the destination role.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "role_key": "string",
  "to_role_key": "string"
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» role_key|body|string|true|The key of the role to remove from the role set|
|» to_role_key|body|string|true|The key of the role to reassign members to|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-phone-numbers">Phone Numbers</h1>

A user can be associated with one or more phone numbers, which allows them to be contacted via SMS.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/references/javascript/types/phone-number">External documentation</a>

## Create a phone number

<a id="opIdCreatePhoneNumber"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/phone_numbers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "string",
    "phone_number": "string",
    "verified": true,
    "primary": true,
    "reserved_for_second_factor": true
  }'
```

`POST /phone_numbers`

Create a new phone number

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_id": "string",
  "phone_number": "string",
  "verified": true,
  "primary": true,
  "reserved_for_second_factor": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-phone-number-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» user_id|body|string|true|The ID representing the user|
|» phone_number|body|string|true|The new phone number. Must adhere to the E.164 standard for phone number format.|
|» verified|body|boolean \| null|false|When created, the phone number will be marked as verified.|
|» primary|body|boolean \| null|false|Create this phone number as the primary phone number for the user. Default: false, unless it is the first phone number.|
|» reserved_for_second_factor|body|boolean \| null|false|Create this phone number as reserved for multi-factor authentication. The phone number must also be verified.<br>If there are no other reserved second factors, the phone number will be set as the default second factor.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "object": "phone_number",
  "phone_number": "string",
  "reserved_for_second_factor": true,
  "default_second_factor": true,
```

## Send a verification code to a phone number

<a id="opIdPreparePhoneNumberVerification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/phone_numbers/string/prepare_verification \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /phone_numbers/{phone_number_id}/prepare_verification`

Sends a one-time code to the given phone number so that a backend can
verify the user controls it (for example, in a custom, backend-driven
sign-in flow). The code is tracked on its own verification; confirm it
with attempt_verification.

## Verify a code sent to a phone number

<a id="opIdAttemptPhoneNumberVerification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/phone_numbers/string/attempt_verification \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "verification_id": "string",
    "code": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /phone_numbers/{phone_number_id}/attempt_verification`

Checks a one-time code against the verification identified by
verification_id, and returns the verification with its updated status
(`verified`, `unverified`, `expired`, or `failed`) and attempt count, so a
backend driving its own frontend can react on every attempt — an incorrect
or expired code is reported through the status, not as an error. Resubmitting
a verification whose code was already accepted is rejected with a
`verification_already_verified` error. If the code for this verification
could not be sent (the SMS provider refused or failed the send after
prepare_verification had returned), the attempt is rejected with a
`verification_code_not_sent` error and no attempt is counted; call
prepare_verification again to send a new code. If too many codes have been
checked for this phone number recently, the attempt is rejected with a
`verification_code_too_many_attempts` error and no attempt is counted; the
limit is per phone number, so wait for the `Retry-After` period rather than
sending a new code. If the code
is correct and the phone number is not already verified, it is also marked
as verified as a side effect (just as it would be in a frontend verification
flow); an already verified phone number is left unchanged. It never creates
a session; to sign the user in afterwards, mint a sign-in token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "verification_id": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-a-code-sent-to-a-phone-number-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|phone_number_id|path|string|true|The ID of the phone number whose code is being verified|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» verification_id|body|string|true|The ID of the verification to check, such as one returned by prepare_verification|
|» code|body|string|true|The verification code that was sent to the phone number|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "strategy": "string",
  "attempts": 0,
  "expire_at": 0,
  "channel": "string"
}
```

```json
}
```

## Replace a user's phone number

<a id="opIdReplaceUserPhoneNumber"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/phone_number \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "phone_number": "string",
    "identification_status": "verified"
  }'
```

`PUT /users/{user_id}/phone_number`

Replaces all of the user's phone numbers with a single primary phone number.
By default the new phone number is created verified, with the admin verification strategy.
When `identification_status` is `reserved` it is created reserved instead: unverified but usable
for sign-in and locked so no other user can claim it. When it is `unverified` the phone number is
neither usable for sign-in nor locked. The new phone number is never reserved for
second factor. Any existing phone numbers are deleted; replacing a phone number that is reserved
for second factor disables the user's MFA.

**Warning:** `identification_status: unverified` can lock the user out of their account. An
unverified phone number cannot be used to sign in, so if the user has no other verified or
reserved identifier, deleting their existing phone numbers leaves them unable to authenticate —
and unable to verify the new number, since that requires signing in. Recovery then requires
another admin API call.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "phone_number": "string",
  "identification_status": "verified"
}
```

<h3 id="replace-a-users-phone-number-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user whose phone number to replace|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» phone_number|body|string|true|The new phone number. Must adhere to the E.164 standard for phone number format.|
|» identification_status|body|string|false|Controls the status of the replacement phone number. Defaults to `verified`. Set to<br>`reserved` to create it reserved (unverified but usable for sign-in and locked so no<br>other user can claim it), or to `unverified` to create it neither usable for sign-in<br>nor locked.<br><br>**Warning:** `unverified` can lock the user out of their account. An unverified phone<br>number cannot be used to sign in, so if the user has no other verified or reserved<br>identifier, they will be unable to authenticate and unable to verify this number.<br>Prefer `reserved` unless you specifically need the number left unclaimed — for<br>example so that another user can also hold it until one of them verifies it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» identification_status|verified|
|» identification_status|reserved|
|» identification_status|unverified|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "object": "phone_number",
  "phone_number": "string",
  "reserved_for_second_factor": true,
  "default_second_factor": true,
  "reserved": true,

    "object": "verification_otp",

    "verified_at_client": "string"
  },

    {
      "type": "string",

    }
  ],
```

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-redirect-urls">Redirect URLs</h1>

Redirect URLs are whitelisted URLs that facilitate secure authentication flows in native applications (e.g. React Native, Expo).
In these contexts, Clerk ensures that security-critical nonces are passed only to the whitelisted URLs.

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-saml-connections">SAML Connections</h1>

A SAML Connection holds configuration data required for facilitating a SAML SSO flow between your
Clerk Instance (SP) and a particular SAML IdP.

## Get a list of SAML Connections for an instance

<a id="opIdListSAMLConnections"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/saml_connections \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /saml_connections`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns the list of SAML Connections for an instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.
The SAML Connections are ordered by descending creation date and the most recent will be returned first.
Deprecated: Use the Enterprise Connections API instead. This endpoint will be removed in future versions.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-saml-connections-for-an-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|
|query|query|string|false|Returns SAML connections that have a name that matches the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Sorts organizations memberships by phone_number, email_address, created_at, first_name, last_name or username.<br>By prepending one of those values with + or -,<br>we can choose to sort in ascending (ASC) or descending (DESC) order.|
|organization_id|query|[string]|false|Returns SAML connections that have an associated organization ID to the<br>given organizations.<br>For each organization ID, the `+` and `-` can be<br>prepended to the ID, which denote whether the<br>respective organization should be included or<br>excluded from the result set.<br>Accepts up to 100 organization IDs.|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-enterprise-connections">Enterprise Connections</h1>

An Enterprise Connection holds configuration data required for facilitating an enterprise SSO flow between your
Clerk instance and an identity provider.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/guides/configure/auth-strategies/enterprise-connections/overview">External documentation</a>

## List enterprise connections

<a id="opIdListEnterpriseConnections"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/enterprise_connections \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /enterprise_connections`

Returns the list of enterprise connections for the instance.
Results can be paginated using the optional `limit` and `offset` query parameters.

<h3 id="list-enterprise-connections-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|
|organization_id|query|string|false|Filter enterprise connections by organization ID|
|active|query|boolean|false|Filter by active status. If true, only active connections are returned. If false, only inactive connections are returned. If omitted, all connections are returned.|

<h3 id="create-an-enterprise-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The display name of the connection|
|» provider|body|string|true|The identity provider (e.g. saml_custom, oidc_custom, oidc_github_enterprise, oidc_gitlab)|
|» domains|body|[string]|true|Domains associated with the enterprise connection (required; at least one). Values are normalized to lowercase. Each domain must be a valid fully qualified domain name.|
|» organization_id|body|string \| null|false|Organization ID when the connection is linked to an organization|
|» allow_organization_account_linking|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether this connection supports account linking via organization membership|
|» active|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the enterprise connection is active. When true, IdP metadata must be provided via the `saml` object.|
|» saml|body|object \| null|false|SAML connection-specific properties. Only applied when the enterprise connection uses SAML (e.g. provider is saml_custom).<br>Use this to set IdP configuration, attribute mapping, and other SAML-specific settings at creation time.|
|» » idp_entity_id|body|string \| null|false|IdP entity ID|
|» » idp_sso_url|body|string \| null|false|IdP SSO URL|
|» » idp_certificate|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use idp_certificates. One X.509 certificate, PEM or bare base64, or several concatenated PEM certificates; replaces the connection's whole certificate set|
|» » idp_certificates|body|[string]|false|The IdP X.509 signing certificates the connection trusts, one per entry, in PEM or bare base64. Replaces the connection's whole certificate set and takes precedence over idp_certificate|
|» » idp_metadata_url|body|string \| null|false|URL to IdP metadata|
|» » idp_metadata|body|string \| null|false|Raw IdP metadata XML|
|» » attribute_mapping|body|object \| null|false|Attribute mapping for SAML attributes|
|» » » user_id|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » » email_address|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » » first_name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » » last_name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » allow_subdomains|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » allow_idp_initiated|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » force_authn|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » login_hint|body|object \| null|false|Configuration for the login_hint sent to the IdP on SSO sign-in|
|» » » mode|body|string|true|Controls the login_hint sent to the IdP on SSO sign-in|
|» » » source|body|string|false|The user public_metadata key whose value is sent as the login_hint when mode is custom_attribute|
|» oidc|body|object \| null|false|OIDC connection-specific properties. Only applied when the enterprise connection uses OIDC (e.g. provider is oidc_custom, oidc_github_enterprise, or oidc_gitlab).|
|» » client_id|body|string \| null|false|OIDC client ID|
|» » client_secret|body|string \| null|false|OIDC client secret|
|» » discovery_url|body|string \| null|false|OIDC discovery URL|
|» » auth_url|body|string \| null|false|OIDC authorization URL|
|» » token_url|body|string \| null|false|OIDC token URL|
|» » user_info_url|body|string \| null|false|OIDC userinfo URL|
|» » requires_pkce|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether PKCE is required (must be true for public clients with no client secret)|
|» custom_attributes|body|[object]|false|Custom attributes to map from the IdP to the user's profile via SSO or SCIM provisioning. Requires the custom attributes feature to be enabled for the instance.|
|» » name|body|string|true|Display name for the custom attribute|
|» » key|body|string|true|Key used to store the attribute in the user's metadata|
|» » sso_path|body|string|false|Path to extract the attribute value from SSO claims|
|» » scim_path|body|string|false|GJSON path to extract the attribute value from SCIM user resources|
|» » directory_path|body|string|false|The new name for `scim_path`. Send either one, or both with the same value; sending both with different values is rejected.|
|» » multi_valued|body|boolean|false|When true, the attribute supports multiple values; values from the IdP are written to public_metadata as an array. Defaults to false.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» provider|saml_custom|
|» provider|saml_okta|
|» provider|saml_google|
|» provider|saml_microsoft|
|» provider|oidc_custom|
|» provider|oidc_github_enterprise|
|» provider|oidc_gitlab|
|» » » mode|email_address|
|» » » mode|custom_attribute|
|» » » mode|off|

`PATCH /enterprise_connections/{enterprise_connection_id}`

Updates the enterprise connection whose ID matches the provided `enterprise_connection_id` in the path.
When enabling the connection (setting `active` to true), any existing verified organization domains that match the connection's domains (e.g. used for enrollment modes like automatic invitation) may be deleted so the connection can be enabled.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "domains": [
    "string"
  ],
  "active": true,
  "sync_user_attributes": true,
  "disable_additional_identifications": true,
  "allow_organization_account_linking": true,
  "organization_id": "string",
  "saml": {
    "name": "string",
    "idp_entity_id": "string",
    "idp_sso_url": "string",
    "idp_certificate": "string",
    "idp_certificates": [

    ],
```

<h3 id="update-an-enterprise-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise_connection_id|path|string|true|The ID of the enterprise connection to update|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|The display name of the enterprise connection|
|» domains|body|[string]|false|Domains associated with the enterprise connection. Values are normalized to lowercase.<br>Empty array means ignored (no change); non-empty array means set domains to the given list (replaces existing).|
|» active|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the enterprise connection is active. When set to true (enabling), any existing verified organization domains for the same domain(s) will be removed so the connection can be enabled.|
|» sync_user_attributes|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to sync user attributes on sign-in|
|» disable_additional_identifications|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to disable additional identifications|
|» allow_organization_account_linking|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether this connection supports account linking via organization membership|
|» organization_id|body|string \| null|false|Organization ID to link to this enterprise connection. Only linking is supported; sending this field sets or changes the linked organization. There is no way to unlink an organization once linked.|
|» saml|body|object \| null|false|SAML connection-specific properties. Only applied when the enterprise connection uses SAML.<br>Use this to update IdP configuration, attribute mapping, and other SAML-specific settings.|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|Display name of the SAML connection|
|» » idp_entity_id|body|string \| null|false|IdP entity ID|
|» » idp_sso_url|body|string \| null|false|IdP SSO URL|
|» » idp_certificate|body|string \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated, use idp_certificates. One X.509 certificate, PEM or bare base64, or several concatenated PEM certificates; replaces the connection's whole certificate set|
|» » idp_certificates|body|[string]|false|The IdP X.509 signing certificates the connection trusts, one per entry, in PEM or bare base64. Replaces the connection's whole certificate set and takes precedence over idp_certificate|
|» » idp_metadata_url|body|string \| null|false|URL to IdP metadata|
|» » idp_metadata|body|string \| null|false|Raw IdP metadata XML|
|» » attribute_mapping|body|object \| null|false|Attribute mapping for SAML attributes|
|» » » user_id|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » » email_address|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » » first_name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » » last_name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » allow_subdomains|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » allow_idp_initiated|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » force_authn|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » login_hint|body|object \| null|false|Configuration for the login_hint sent to the IdP on SSO sign-in|
|» » » mode|body|string|true|Controls the login_hint sent to the IdP on SSO sign-in|
|» » » source|body|string|false|The user public_metadata key whose value is sent as the login_hint when mode is custom_attribute|
|» oidc|body|object \| null|false|OIDC connection-specific properties. Only applied when the enterprise connection uses OIDC (e.g. oidc_custom, oidc_github_enterprise, or oidc_gitlab).|
|» » client_id|body|string \| null|false|OIDC client ID|
|» » client_secret|body|string \| null|false|OIDC client secret|
|» » discovery_url|body|string \| null|false|OIDC discovery URL|
|» » auth_url|body|string \| null|false|OIDC authorization URL|
|» » token_url|body|string \| null|false|OIDC token URL|
|» » user_info_url|body|string \| null|false|OIDC userinfo URL|
|» » requires_pkce|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether PKCE is required (must be true for public clients with no client secret)|
|» custom_attributes|body|[object]|false|Custom attributes to map from the IdP to the user's profile via SSO or SCIM provisioning. Requires the custom attributes feature to be enabled for the instance.|
|» » name|body|string|true|Display name for the custom attribute|
|» » key|body|string|true|Key used to store the attribute in the user's metadata|
|» » sso_path|body|string|false|Path to extract the attribute value from SSO claims|
|» » scim_path|body|string|false|GJSON path to extract the attribute value from SCIM user resources|
|» » directory_path|body|string|false|The new name for `scim_path`. Send either one, or both with the same value; sending both with different values is rejected.|
|» » multi_valued|body|boolean|false|When true, the attribute supports multiple values; values from the IdP are written to public_metadata as an array. Defaults to false.|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-sessions">Sessions</h1>

The Session object is an abstraction over an HTTP session.
It models the period of information exchange between a user and the server.
Sessions are created when a user successfully goes through the sign in or sign up flows.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/references/javascript/session">External documentation</a>

## List all sessions

<a id="opIdGetSessionList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/sessions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /sessions`

Returns a list of sessions matching the provided criteria.
The sessions are returned sorted by creation date, with the newest sessions appearing first.

Note: This endpoint does not return all sessions that have ever existed. Old and inactive sessions are periodically cleaned up and will not be included in the results.

**Deprecation Notice (2024-01-01):** All parameters were initially considered optional, however
moving forward at least one of `client_id` or `user_id` parameters should be provided.

<h3 id="list-all-sessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|query|string|false|List sessions for the given client|
|user_id|query|string|false|List sessions for the given user|
|status|query|string|false|Filter sessions by the provided status|
|paginated|query|boolean|false|Whether to paginate the results.<br>If true, the results will be paginated.<br>If false, the results will not be paginated.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|abandoned|
|status|active|
|status|ended|
|status|expired|
|status|removed|
|status|replaced|
|status|revoked|

## Create a new active session

<a id="opIdcreateSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "string",
    "active_organization_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sessions`

Create a new active session for the provided user ID.

**This operation is intended only for use in testing, and is not available for production instances.** If you are looking to generate a user session from the backend,
we recommend using the [Sign-in Tokens](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend-api/tag/Sign-in-Tokens#operation/CreateSignInToken) resource instead.

## Refresh a session

<a id="opIdRefreshSession"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

    "expired_token": "string",

    "request_originating_ip": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sessions/{session_id}/refresh`

Refreshes a session by creating a new session token. A 401 is returned when there
are validation errors, which signals the SDKs to fall back to the handshake flow.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expired_token": "string",
  "refresh_token": "string",
  "request_origin": "string",
  "request_headers": {},
  "format": "token",
  "request_originating_ip": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The ID of the session|
|body|body|object|false|Refresh session parameters|
|» expired_token|body|string|true|The JWT that is sent via the `__session` cookie from your frontend.<br>Note: this JWT must be associated with the supplied session ID.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|true|The refresh token from the `__refresh` cookie set via FAPI's handshake flow.|
|» request_origin|body|string|true|The origin of the request.|
|» request_headers|body|object \| null|false|The headers of the request.|
|» format|body|string \| null|false|The format of the response.|
|» request_originating_ip|body|string \| null|false|The IP address of the request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

## Retrieve a reverification

<a id="opIdGetReverification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/sessions/string/reverifications/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /sessions/{session_id}/reverifications/{reverification_id}`

Retrieve a reverification scoped to a session. A resource server can use this to validate a reverification id it received from its client: confirm it is real, scoped to the expected session, completed, and how fresh each factor is. Single-use / replay detection is the caller's responsibility (the id is stable, so the caller dedups consumed ids).

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-machines">Machines</h1>

A Machine represents a machine/server/service which can be used in machine-to-machine authentication.

## Get a list of machines for an instance

<a id="opIdListMachines"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/machines \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /machines`

This request returns the list of machines for an instance. The machines are
ordered by descending creation date (i.e. most recent machines will be
returned first)

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-machines-for-an-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|
|query|query|string|false|Returns machines with ID or name that match the given query. Uses exact match for machine ID and partial match for name.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Allows to return machines in a particular order.<br>You can order the returned machines by their `name` or `created_at`.<br>To specify the direction, use the `+` or `-` symbols prepended to the property to order by.<br>For example, to return machines in descending order by `created_at`, use `-created_at`.<br>If you don't use `+` or `-`, then `+` is implied.<br>Defaults to `-created_at`.|

## Rotate a machine's secret key

<a id="opIdRotateMachineSecretKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/machines/string/secret_key/rotate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "previous_token_ttl": 0
  }'
```

`POST /machines/{machine_id}/secret_key/rotate`

Rotates the machine's secret key.
When the secret key is rotated, make sure to update it in your machine/application.
The previous secret key will remain valid for the duration specified by the previous_token_ttl parameter.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "previous_token_ttl": 0
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|machine_id|path|string|true|The ID of the machine to rotate the secret key for|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» previous_token_ttl|body|integer|true|The time in seconds that the previous secret key will remain valid after rotation.<br>This ensures a graceful transition period for updating applications with the new secret key.<br>Set to 0 to immediately expire the previous key. Maximum value is 8 hours (28800 seconds).|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-m2m-tokens">M2M Tokens</h1>

Machine to Machine Tokens are used to manage authentication between Machines.

## Get M2M Tokens

<a id="opIdgetM2MTokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.clerk.com/v1/m2m_tokens?subject=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /m2m_tokens`

Fetches M2M tokens for a specific machine.

Only tokens created with the opaque token format are returned by this endpoint. JWT-format M2M tokens are stateless and are not stored.

This endpoint can be authenticated by either a Machine Secret Key or by a Clerk Secret Key.

- When fetching M2M tokens with a Machine Secret Key, only tokens associated with the authenticated machine can be retrieved.
- When fetching M2M tokens with a Clerk Secret Key, tokens for any machine in the instance can be retrieved.

<h3 id="get-m2m-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subject|query|string|true|none|
|revoked|query|boolean \| null|false|none|
|expired|query|boolean \| null|false|none|
|limit|query|number|false|none|
|offset|query|number \| null|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "m2m_tokens": [
    {
      "object": "machine_to_machine_token",
      "id": "mt_f7f0ba8c3b4843ce7d85fcdd5e71853e",
      "subject": "mch_2xhFjEI5X2qWRvtV13BzSj8H6Dk",
      "claims": {
        "important_metadata": "Some useful data"
      },
      "scopes": [
        "mch_2xhFjEI5X2qWRvtV13BzSj8H6Dk",
        "mch_2yGkLpQ7Y3rXSwtU24CzTk9I7Em"
      ],
      "revoked": false,
      "revocation_reason": "Revoked by user",
      "expired": false,
      "expiration": 1716883200000,
      "last_used_at": 1716883200000,
      "created_at": 1716883200000,
      "updated_at": 1716883200000
    }
  ],
  "total_count": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
```

## Create a M2M Token

<a id="opIdcreateM2MToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/m2m_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "token_format": "opaque",
    "seconds_until_expiration": 0.1,
    "claims": null,
    "min_remaining_ttl_seconds": 240
  }'
```

`POST /m2m_tokens`

Creates a new M2M Token. Must be authenticated via a Machine Secret Key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "token_format": "opaque",
  "seconds_until_expiration": 0.1,
  "claims": null,
  "min_remaining_ttl_seconds": 240
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-m2m-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» token_format|body|string|false|none|
|» seconds_until_expiration|body|number \| null|false|none|
|» claims|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» min_remaining_ttl_seconds|body|integer|false|Enables server-side token reuse for opaque-format tokens. When set, if a non-revoked, non-expired M2M token already exists for this machine with identical `claims` and `scopes` and at least this many seconds of remaining lifetime, that existing token is returned and no new token is minted.<br><br>Use this when caching tokens in application memory across requests is impractical — for example, in serverless functions, short-lived job workers, or autoscaling containers that churn faster than the token TTL. Pooling at the server collapses many redundant create calls into reuse of a single live token, which is the recommended pattern for high-volume M2M traffic.<br><br>Must be strictly less than the effective token lifetime — that is, `seconds_until_expiration` when provided, or the machine's default TTL otherwise. A value greater than or equal to the lifetime is rejected with a 400, since no freshly-minted token would ever satisfy the requirement.<br><br>Only applies to opaque-format tokens (`token_format` defaults to `opaque`). JWT-format tokens are stateless and are never deduplicated.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» token_format|opaque|
|» token_format|jwt|

## Revoke a M2M Token

<a id="opIdrevokeM2MToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/m2m_tokens/string/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "revocation_reason": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /m2m_tokens/{m2m_token_id}/revoke`

Revokes a M2M Token.

This endpoint only revokes stored opaque-format M2M tokens. JWT-format M2M tokens are stateless and cannot be revoked.

This endpoint can be authenticated by either a Machine Secret Key or by a Clerk Secret Key.

- When revoking a M2M Token with a Machine Secret Key, the token must managed by the Machine associated with the Machine Secret Key.
- When revoking a M2M Token with a Clerk Secret Key, any token on the Instance can be revoked.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "revocation_reason": "string"
}
```

|m2m_token_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» revocation_reason|body|string \| null|false|none|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-sign-in-tokens">Sign-in Tokens</h1>

Sign-in tokens are JWTs that can be used to sign in to an application without specifying any credentials.
A sign-in token can be used at most once and they can be consumed from the Frontend API using the `ticket` strategy.

## Create sign-in token

<a id="opIdCreateSignInToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/sign_in_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "string",
    "org_id": "string",
    "expires_in_seconds": 1,
    "second_factor_verification": "fresh"
  }'
```

`POST /sign_in_tokens`

Creates a new sign-in token and associates it with the given user.
By default, sign-in tokens expire in 30 days.
You can optionally supply a different duration in seconds using the `expires_in_seconds` property.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_id": "string",
  "org_id": "string",
  "expires_in_seconds": 1,
  "second_factor_verification": "fresh"
}
```

<h3 id="create-sign-in-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» user_id|body|string|true|The ID of the user that can use the newly created sign in token|
|» org_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the organization to activate when the user signs in.<br>Organizations must be enabled for the instance, and the user must be a member of the organization.|
|» expires_in_seconds|body|integer \| null|false|Optional parameter to specify the life duration of the sign in token in seconds.<br>By default, the duration is 30 days, or 10 minutes when `second_factor_verification` is set.|
|» second_factor_verification|body|string \| null|false|Optional parameter that lets a user with a second factor enabled complete the sign in without being prompted for it.<br>When omitted, redeeming the token completes only the first factor, and the user must still complete their second factor.<br>`fresh`: the second factor is treated as verified at sign in. The session token's `fva` claim reports a second factor age of 0.<br>`stale`: the second factor is treated as unverified. The session token's `fva` claim reports the maximum second factor age of 99999, so any reverification that requires a second factor prompts the user to complete one.<br>Has no effect for users without a second factor enabled.<br>A token created with this parameter signs in a user with a second factor enabled without prompting for it, so `expires_in_seconds` defaults to 10 minutes. We recommend keeping it short.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» second_factor_verification|fresh|
|» second_factor_verification|stale|

```json
}
```

```json
    }
```

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-users">Users</h1>

The user object represents a user that has successfully signed up to your application.

<a href="https://clerk.com/docs/references/javascript/user">External documentation</a>

## List all users

<a id="opIdGetUserList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users`

Returns a list of all users.
The users are returned sorted by creation date, with the newest users appearing first.

To walk more than a few pages, paginate with `starting_after` rather than `offset`.
A cursor page costs the same no matter how far into the list it sits, while a large `offset`
has to walk and discard every row before it, so it gets progressively slower and eventually
times out. Cursor pagination requires the `created_at` ordering, which is the default.

<h3 id="list-all-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email_address|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified email addresses.<br>Accepts up to 100 email addresses.<br>Any email addresses not found are ignored.|
|phone_number|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified phone numbers.<br>Accepts up to 100 phone numbers.<br>Any phone numbers not found are ignored.|
|external_id|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified external IDs.<br>For each external ID, the `+` and `-` can be<br>prepended to the ID, which denote whether the<br>respective external ID should be included or<br>excluded from the result set.<br>Accepts up to 100 external IDs.<br>Any external IDs not found are ignored.|
|username|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified usernames.<br>Accepts up to 100 usernames.<br>Any usernames not found are ignored.|
|web3_wallet|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified web3 wallet addresses.<br>Accepts up to 100 web3 wallet addresses.<br>Any web3 wallet addresses not found are ignored.|
|user_id|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the user IDs specified.<br>For each user ID, the `+` and `-` can be<br>prepended to the ID, which denote whether the<br>respective user ID should be included or<br>excluded from the result set.<br>Accepts up to 100 user IDs.<br>Any user IDs not found are ignored.|
|organization_id|query|[string]|false|Returns users that have memberships to the<br>given organizations.<br>For each organization ID, the `+` and `-` can be<br>prepended to the ID, which denote whether the<br>respective organization should be included or<br>excluded from the result set.<br>Accepts up to 100 organization IDs.|
|query|query|string|false|Returns users that match the given query.<br>For possible matches, we check the email addresses, phone numbers, usernames, web3 wallets, user IDs, first and last names.<br>The query value doesn't need to match the exact value you are looking for, it is capable of partial matches as well.|
|email_address_query|query|string|false|Returns users with emails that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>For example, `email_address_query=ello` will match a user with the email `HELLO@example.com`.|
|phone_number_query|query|string|false|Returns users with phone numbers that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>For example, `phone_number_query=555` will match a user with the phone number `+1555xxxxxxx`.|
|username_query|query|string|false|Returns users with usernames that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>For example, `username_query=CoolUser` will match a user with the username `SomeCoolUser`.|
|name_query|query|string|false|Returns users with names that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.|
|banned|query|boolean|false|Returns users which are either banned (`banned=true`) or not banned (`banned=false`).|
|last_active_at_before|query|integer|false|Returns users whose last session activity was before the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users whose last session activity was before 2023-11-23.|
|last_active_at_after|query|integer|false|Returns users whose last session activity was after the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users whose last session activity was after 2023-11-23.|
|last_active_at_since|query|integer|false|**Deprecated.** Returns users that had session activity since the given date.<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users that had session activity from 2023-11-23 until the current day.<br>Deprecated in favor of `last_active_at_after`.|
|created_at_before|query|integer|false|Returns users who have been created before the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1730160000000 to retrieve users who have been created before 2024-10-29.|
|created_at_after|query|integer|false|Returns users who have been created after the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1730160000000 to retrieve users who have been created after 2024-10-29.|
|last_sign_in_at_before|query|integer|false|Returns users whose last sign-in was before the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users whose last sign-in was before 2023-11-23.|
|last_sign_in_at_after|query|integer|false|Returns users whose last sign-in was after the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users whose last sign-in was after 2023-11-23.|
|provider|query|string|false|Returns users with external accounts for the specified OAuth provider.<br>Must be used in combination with the `provider_user_id` parameter.<br>For example, use `provider=oauth_google&provider_user_id=12345` to retrieve a user with Google provider user ID 12345.|
|provider_user_id|query|[string]|false|Returns users with the specified provider user IDs for a specific provider.<br>Must be used in combination with the `provider` parameter.<br>For example, use `provider=oauth_google&provider_user_id=12345` to retrieve a user with Google provider user ID 12345.<br>Accepts up to 100 provider user IDs.<br>Any provider user IDs not found are ignored.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|A cursor for pagination: the `id` of the last user on the previous page. Returns the users that follow it.<br><br>**Requires ordering by `created_at`** — that is, `order_by` omitted, or set to `created_at`, `+created_at`<br>or `-created_at`. Any other `order_by` value is rejected with a 422: the other orderings sort by a value<br>that is neither unique per user nor immutable, so a cursor over them would skip or repeat users.<br><br>Cannot be combined with a non-zero `offset`, which is also a 422. Keep every other parameter identical<br>across requests, and stop when a page returns fewer than `limit` users.|
|order_by|query|string|false|Allows to return users in a particular order.<br>At the moment, you can order the returned users by their `created_at`,`updated_at`,`email_address`,`web3wallet`,`first_name`,`last_name`,`phone_number`,`username`,`last_active_at`,`last_sign_in_at`.<br>In order to specify the direction, you can use the `+/-` symbols prepended in the property to order by.<br>For example, if you want users to be returned in descending order according to their `created_at` property, you can use `-created_at`.<br>If you don't use `+` or `-`, then `+` is implied. We only support one `order_by` parameter, and if multiple `order_by` parameters are provided, we will only keep the first one. For example,<br>if you pass `order_by=username&order_by=created_at`, we will consider only the first `order_by` parameter, which is `username`. The `created_at` parameter will be ignored in this case.<br>Only the `created_at` orderings can be combined with `starting_after` cursor pagination; see that parameter.|

> 200 Response

## Create a new user

<a id="opIdCreateUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "external_id": "string",
    "first_name": "string",
    "last_name": "string",
    "locale": "string",
    "timezone": "string",
    "email_address": [
      "string"
    ],
    "email_address_identification_status": [
      "verified"
    ],
    "phone_number": [
      "string"
    ],
    "phone_number_identification_status": [
      "verified"
    ],
    "web3_wallet": [
      "string"
    ],
    "username": "string",
    "password": "string",
    "password_digest": "string",
    "password_hasher": "string",
    "skip_password_checks": true,
    "skip_password_requirement": true,
    "skip_restriction_checks": true,
    "totp_secret": "string",
    "backup_codes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "public_metadata": {},
    "private_metadata": {},
    "unsafe_metadata": {},
    "delete_self_enabled": true,
    "legal_accepted_at": "string",
    "skip_legal_checks": true,
    "skip_user_requirement": true,
    "create_organization_enabled": true,
    "create_organizations_limit": 0,
    "created_at": "string",
    "bypass_client_trust": true,
    "banned": true,
    "locked": true
  }'
```

`POST /users`

Creates a new user. Your user management settings determine how you should setup your user model.

By default, any email address and phone number created using this method is marked as verified. Use the `email_address_identification_status` and `phone_number_identification_status` arrays to instead create some or all of them as reserved (unverified but usable for sign-in and locked so no other user can claim them).

Note: If you are performing a migration, check out our guide on [zero downtime migrations](https://clerk.com/docs/deployments/migrate-overview).

The following rate limit rules apply to this endpoint: 1000 requests per 10 seconds for production instances and 100 requests per 10 seconds for development instances

```json
  ],
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the user as used in your external systems or your previous authentication solution.<br>Must be unique across your instance.|
|» first_name|body|string \| null|false|The first name to assign to the user|
|» last_name|body|string \| null|false|The last name to assign to the user|
|» locale|body|string \| null|false|The locale to assign to the user (e.g., "en-US", "fr-FR")|
|» timezone|body|string \| null|false|The IANA timezone to assign to the user (e.g., "America/New_York", "Europe/Paris"). Set to null to clear it and allow automatic capture on a later trusted sign-in.|
|» email_address|body|[string]|false|Email addresses to add to the user.<br>Must be unique across your instance.<br>The first email address will be set as the user's primary email address.<br>Created verified by default; see `email_address_identification_status` to create them reserved.|
|» email_address_identification_status|body|[string]|false|Controls the status each email address is created with. Runs parallel to<br>`email_address`: when provided, it must contain exactly one item per email<br>address, applied by position. When omitted or empty, every email address is<br>created `verified`. Set an item to `reserved` to create the corresponding<br>email address reserved instead (unverified but usable for sign-in and locked<br>so no other user can claim it).|
|» phone_number|body|[string]|false|Phone numbers to add to the user.<br>Must be unique across your instance.<br>The first phone number will be set as the user's primary phone number.<br>Created verified by default; see `phone_number_identification_status` to create them reserved.|
|» phone_number_identification_status|body|[string]|false|Controls the status each phone number is created with. Runs parallel to<br>`phone_number`: when provided, it must contain exactly one item per phone<br>number, applied by position. When omitted or empty, every phone number is<br>created `verified`. Set an item to `reserved` to create the corresponding<br>phone number reserved instead (unverified but usable for sign-in and locked<br>so no other user can claim it).|
|» web3_wallet|body|[string]|false|Web3 wallets to add to the user.<br>Must be unique across your instance.<br>The first wallet will be set as the user's primary wallet.|
|» username|body|string \| null|false|The username to give to the user.<br>It must be unique across your instance.|
|» password|body|string \| null|false|The plaintext password to give the user.<br>Must be at least 8 characters long, and cannot be in any list of hacked passwords.|
|» password_digest|body|string \| null|false|In case you already have the password digests and not the passwords, you can use them for the newly created user via this property.<br>The digests should be generated with one of the supported algorithms.<br>The hashing algorithm can be specified using the `password_hasher` property.|
|» password_hasher|body|[PasswordHasher](#schemapasswordhasher)|false|The hashing algorithm that was used to generate the password digest.<br><br>The algorithms we support at the moment are [`bcrypt`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bcrypt), [`bcrypt_sha256_django`](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.0/topics/auth/passwords/), [`md5`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MD5), `pbkdf2_sha1`, `pbkdf2_sha256`, [`pbkdf2_sha256_django`](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.0/topics/auth/passwords/),<br>`pbkdf2_sha512`, [`phpass`](https://www.openwall.com/phpass/), `md5_phpass`, [`scrypt_firebase`](https://firebaseopensource.com/projects/firebase/scrypt/),<br>[`scrypt_werkzeug`](https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/en/3.0.x/utils/#werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash), [`sha256`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2),<br>[`ldap_ssha`](https://www.openldap.org/faq/data/cache/347.html), the [`argon2`](https://argon2.online/) variants: `argon2i` and `argon2id`, `sha512_symfony`, the SHA-512 variant of the [Symfony](https://symfony.com/doc/current/security/passwords.html) legacy hasher,<br>and `pbkdf2_sha512_hex`, a variant of `pbkdf2_sha512` that accepts hex-encoded salt and hash.<br><br>Each of the supported hashers expects the incoming digest to be in a particular format. See the [Clerk docs](https://clerk.com/docs/references/backend/user/create-user) for more information.|
|» skip_password_checks|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true` all password checks are skipped.<br>It is recommended to use this method only when migrating plaintext passwords to Clerk.<br>Upon migration the user base should be prompted to pick stronger password.|
|» skip_password_requirement|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true`, `password` is not required anymore when creating the user and can be omitted.<br>This is useful when you are trying to create a user that doesn't have a password, in an instance that is using passwords.<br>Please note that you cannot use this flag if password is the only way for a user to sign into your instance.|
|» skip_restriction_checks|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true`, the instance's restrictions are not applied to this user.<br>Those settings are the allowlist, the blocklist, blocked disposable email domains and blocked email subaddresses, and they normally reject a matching identifier here just as they do at sign-up.<br>Use this when your backend is creating a user it already trusts, such as during a migration or from an admin tool.|
|» totp_secret|body|string \| null|false|In case TOTP is configured on the instance, you can provide the secret to enable it on the newly created user without the need to reset it.<br>Please note that currently the supported options are:<br>* Period: 30 seconds<br>* Code length: 6 digits<br>* Algorithm: SHA1|
|» backup_codes|body|[string]|false|If Backup Codes are configured on the instance, you can provide them to enable it on the newly created user without the need to reset them.<br>You must provide the backup codes in plain format or the corresponding bcrypt digest.|
|» public_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the user, that is visible to both your Frontend and Backend APIs|
|» private_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the user, that is only visible to your Backend API|
|» unsafe_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the user, that can be updated from both the Frontend and Backend APIs.<br>Note: Since this data can be modified from the frontend, it is not guaranteed to be safe.|
|» delete_self_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|If enabled, user can delete themselves via FAPI.<br>|
|» legal_accepted_at|body|string \| null|false|A custom timestamp denoting _when_ the user accepted legal requirements, specified in RFC3339 format (e.g. `2012-10-20T07:15:20.902Z`).|
|» skip_legal_checks|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true` all legal checks are skipped.<br>It is not recommended to skip legal checks unless you are migrating a user to Clerk.|
|» skip_user_requirement|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true`, identification types are not enforced.<br>At least one identification type must be enabled and provided on your instance (email, phone, web3 wallet, or username).<br>Users created without required identification types cannot use those authentication strategies<br>It is not recommended to use this flag unless you need to allow Clerk UI components to prompt for required fields while BAPI creates users with minimal data, or for migration a user to Clerk.|
|» create_organization_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|If enabled, user can create organizations via FAPI.<br>|
|» create_organizations_limit|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of organizations the user can create. 0 means unlimited.<br>|
|» created_at|body|string \| null|false|A custom date/time denoting _when_ the user signed up to the application, specified in RFC3339 format (e.g. `2012-10-20T07:15:20.902Z`).|
|» bypass_client_trust|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true`, the user will bypass Device Trust checks during sign-in.|
|» banned|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true`, the user is created already banned and cannot sign in.<br>Requires the same plan support as the ban user endpoint.|
|» locked|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true`, the user is created already locked.<br>Requires the user lockout feature to be enabled on the instance.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» email_address_identification_status|verified|
|» email_address_identification_status|reserved|
|» phone_number_identification_status|verified|
|» phone_number_identification_status|reserved|
