## Count users

<a id="opIdGetUsersCount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/count`

Returns a total count of all users that match the given filtering criteria.

<h3 id="count-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email_address|query|[string]|false|Counts users with the specified email addresses.<br>Accepts up to 100 email addresses.<br>Any email addresses not found are ignored.|
|phone_number|query|[string]|false|Counts users with the specified phone numbers.<br>Accepts up to 100 phone numbers.<br>Any phone numbers not found are ignored.|
|external_id|query|[string]|false|Counts users with the specified external IDs.<br>Accepts up to 100 external IDs.<br>Any external IDs not found are ignored.|
|username|query|[string]|false|Counts users with the specified usernames.<br>Accepts up to 100 usernames.<br>Any usernames not found are ignored.|
|web3_wallet|query|[string]|false|Counts users with the specified web3 wallet addresses.<br>Accepts up to 100 web3 wallet addresses.<br>Any web3 wallet addresses not found are ignored.|
|user_id|query|[string]|false|Counts users with the user IDs specified.<br>Accepts up to 100 user IDs.<br>Any user IDs not found are ignored.|
|organization_id|query|[string]|false|Returns users that have memberships to the given organizations. For each organization ID, the `+` and `-`<br>can be prepended to the ID, which denote whether the respective organization should be included or<br>excluded from the result set. Accepts up to 100 organization IDs.|
|query|query|string|false|Counts users that match the given query.<br>For possible matches, we check the email addresses, phone numbers, usernames, web3 wallets, user IDs, first and last names.<br>The query value doesn't need to match the exact value you are looking for, it is capable of partial matches as well.|
|email_address_query|query|string|false|Counts users with emails that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>For example, `email_address_query=ello` will match a user with the email `HELLO@example.com`,<br>and will be included in the resulting count.|
|phone_number_query|query|string|false|Counts users with phone numbers that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>For example, `phone_number_query=555` will match a user with the phone number `+1555xxxxxxx`,<br>and will be included in the resulting count.|
|username_query|query|string|false|Counts users with usernames that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.<br>For example, `username_query=CoolUser` will match a user with the username `SomeCoolUser`,<br>and will be included in the resulting count.|
|name_query|query|string|false|Returns users with names that match the given query, via case-insensitive partial match.|
|banned|query|boolean|false|Counts users which are either banned (`banned=true`) or not banned (`banned=false`).|
|last_active_at_before|query|integer|false|Returns users whose last session activity was before the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users whose last session activity was before 2023-11-23.|
|last_active_at_after|query|integer|false|Returns users whose last session activity was after the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users whose last session activity was after 2023-11-23.|
|last_active_at_since|query|integer|false|**Deprecated.** Returns users that had session activity since the given date.<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to retrieve users that had session activity from 2023-11-23 until the current day.<br>Deprecated in favor of `last_active_at_after`.|
|created_at_before|query|integer|false|Returns users who have been created before the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1730160000000 to retrieve users who have been created before 2024-10-29.|
|created_at_after|query|integer|false|Returns users who have been created after the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1730160000000 to retrieve users who have been created after 2024-10-29.|
|last_sign_in_at_before|query|integer|false|Counts users whose last sign-in was before the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to count users whose last sign-in was before 2023-11-23.|
|last_sign_in_at_after|query|integer|false|Counts users whose last sign-in was after the given date (with millisecond precision).<br>Example: use 1700690400000 to count users whose last sign-in was after 2023-11-23.|
|provider|query|string|false|Counts users with external accounts for the specified OAuth provider.<br>Must be used in combination with the `provider_user_id` parameter.<br>For example, use `provider=oauth_google&provider_user_id=12345` to count users with Google provider user ID 12345.<br>Accepts up to 100 providers.|
|provider_user_id|query|[string]|false|Counts users with the specified provider user IDs for a specific provider.<br>Must be used in combination with the `provider` parameter.<br>For example, use `provider=oauth_google&provider_user_id=12345` to count users with Google provider user ID 12345.<br>Accepts up to 100 provider user IDs.<br>Any provider user IDs not found are ignored.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "total_count",
  "total_count": 0
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "external_id": "string",
    "first_name": "string",
    "last_name": "string",
    "locale": "string",
    "timezone": "string",
    "primary_email_address_id": "string",
    "notify_primary_email_address_changed": false,
    "primary_phone_number_id": "string",
    "primary_web3_wallet_id": "string",
    "username": "string",
```

`PATCH /users/{user_id}`

Update a user's attributes.

You can set the user's primary contact identifiers (email address and phone numbers) by updating the `primary_email_address_id` and `primary_phone_number_id` attributes respectively.
Both IDs should correspond to verified identifications that belong to the user.

You can remove a user's username by setting the username attribute to null or the blank string "".
This is a destructive action; the identification will be deleted forever.
Usernames can be removed only if they are optional in your instance settings and there's at least one other identifier which can be used for authentication.

This endpoint allows changing a user's password. When passing the `password` parameter directly you have two further options.
You can ignore the password policy checks for your instance by setting the `skip_password_checks` parameter to `true`.
You can also choose to sign the user out of all their active sessions on any device once the password is updated. Just set `sign_out_of_other_sessions` to `true`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "external_id": "string",
  "first_name": "string",
  "last_name": "string",
  "locale": "string",
  "timezone": "string",
  "primary_email_address_id": "string",
  "notify_primary_email_address_changed": false,
  "primary_phone_number_id": "string",
  "primary_web3_wallet_id": "string",
  "username": "string",
  "profile_image_id": "string",
  "password": "string",
  "password_digest": "string",
  "password_hasher": "string",
  "skip_password_checks": true,
  "sign_out_of_other_sessions": true,
  "totp_secret": "string",
  "backup_codes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {},
  "unsafe_metadata": {},
  "delete_self_enabled": true,
  "create_organization_enabled": true,
  "legal_accepted_at": "string",
  "skip_legal_checks": true,
  "create_organizations_limit": 0,
  "created_at": "string",
  "bypass_client_trust": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user to update|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the user as used in your external systems or your previous authentication solution.<br>Must be unique across your instance.|
|» first_name|body|string \| null|false|The first name to assign to the user|
|» last_name|body|string \| null|false|The last name to assign to the user|
|» locale|body|string \| null|false|The locale to assign to the user (e.g., "en-US", "fr-FR")|
|» timezone|body|string \| null|false|The IANA timezone to assign to the user (e.g., "America/New_York", "Europe/Paris"). Set to null to clear it and allow automatic capture on a later trusted sign-in.|
|» primary_email_address_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the email address to set as primary.<br>It must be verified, and present on the current user.|
|» notify_primary_email_address_changed|body|boolean \| null|false|If set to `true`, the user will be notified that their primary email address has changed.<br>By default, no notification is sent.|
|» primary_phone_number_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the phone number to set as primary.<br>It must be verified, and present on the current user.|
|» primary_web3_wallet_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the web3 wallets to set as primary.<br>It must be verified, and present on the current user.|
|» username|body|string \| null|false|The username to give to the user.<br>It must be unique across your instance.|
|» profile_image_id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the image to set as the user's profile image|
|» password|body|string \| null|false|The plaintext password to give the user.<br>Must be at least 8 characters long, and cannot be in any list of hacked passwords.|
|» password_digest|body|string|false|In case you already have the password digests and not the passwords, you can use them for the newly created user via this property.<br>The digests should be generated with one of the supported algorithms.<br>The hashing algorithm can be specified using the `password_hasher` property.|
|» password_hasher|body|[PasswordHasher](#schemapasswordhasher)|false|The hashing algorithm that was used to generate the password digest.<br><br>The algorithms we support at the moment are [`bcrypt`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bcrypt), [`bcrypt_sha256_django`](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.0/topics/auth/passwords/), [`md5`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MD5), `pbkdf2_sha1`, `pbkdf2_sha256`, [`pbkdf2_sha256_django`](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.0/topics/auth/passwords/),<br>`pbkdf2_sha512`, [`phpass`](https://www.openwall.com/phpass/), `md5_phpass`, [`scrypt_firebase`](https://firebaseopensource.com/projects/firebase/scrypt/),<br>[`scrypt_werkzeug`](https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/en/3.0.x/utils/#werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash), [`sha256`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2),<br>[`ldap_ssha`](https://www.openldap.org/faq/data/cache/347.html), the [`argon2`](https://argon2.online/) variants: `argon2i` and `argon2id`, `sha512_symfony`, the SHA-512 variant of the [Symfony](https://symfony.com/doc/current/security/passwords.html) legacy hasher,<br>and `pbkdf2_sha512_hex`, a variant of `pbkdf2_sha512` that accepts hex-encoded salt and hash.<br><br>Each of the supported hashers expects the incoming digest to be in a particular format. See the [Clerk docs](https://clerk.com/docs/references/backend/user/create-user) for more information.|
|» skip_password_checks|body|boolean \| null|false|Set it to `true` if you're updating the user's password and want to skip any password policy settings check. This parameter can only be used when providing a `password`.|
|» sign_out_of_other_sessions|body|boolean \| null|false|Set to `true` to sign out the user from all their active sessions once their password is updated. This parameter can only be used when providing a `password`.|
|» totp_secret|body|string \| null|false|In case TOTP is configured on the instance, you can provide the secret to enable it on the specific user without the need to reset it.<br>Please note that currently the supported options are:<br>* Period: 30 seconds<br>* Code length: 6 digits<br>* Algorithm: SHA1|
|» backup_codes|body|[string]|false|If Backup Codes are configured on the instance, you can provide them to enable it on the specific user without the need to reset them.<br>You must provide the backup codes in plain format or the corresponding bcrypt digest.|
|» public_metadata|body|object \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Metadata saved on the user, that is visible to both your Frontend and Backend APIs.<br>Deprecated: As of API version 2026-05-12, this field is rejected on `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}`. Use `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` to merge updates into existing metadata, or `PUT /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` to replace a metadata field entirely.|
|» private_metadata|body|object \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Metadata saved on the user, that is only visible to your Backend API.<br>Deprecated: As of API version 2026-05-12, this field is rejected on `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}`. Use `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` to merge updates into existing metadata, or `PUT /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` to replace a metadata field entirely.|
|» unsafe_metadata|body|object \| null|false|**Deprecated.** Metadata saved on the user, that can be updated from both the Frontend and Backend APIs.<br>Note: Since this data can be modified from the frontend, it is not guaranteed to be safe.<br>Deprecated: As of API version 2026-05-12, this field is rejected on `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}`. Use `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` to merge updates into existing metadata, or `PUT /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` to replace a metadata field entirely.|
|» delete_self_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|If true, the user can delete themselves with the Frontend API.|
|» create_organization_enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|If true, the user can create organizations with the Frontend API.|
|» legal_accepted_at|body|string \| null|false|A custom timestamp denoting _when_ the user accepted legal requirements, specified in RFC3339 format (e.g. `2012-10-20T07:15:20.902Z`).|
|» skip_legal_checks|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true` all legal checks are skipped.<br>It is not recommended to skip legal checks unless you are migrating a user to Clerk.|
|» create_organizations_limit|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of organizations the user can create. 0 means unlimited.|
|» created_at|body|string \| null|false|A custom date/time denoting _when_ the user signed up to the application, specified in RFC3339 format (e.g. `2012-10-20T07:15:20.902Z`).|
|» bypass_client_trust|body|boolean \| null|false|When set to `true`, the user will bypass Device Trust checks during sign-in.|

## Ban a user

<a id="opIdBanUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/ban \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/ban`

Marks the given user as banned, which means that all their sessions are revoked and they are not allowed to sign in again.

<h3 id="ban-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user to ban|

## Ban multiple users

<a id="opIdUsersBan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/ban \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /users/ban`

Marks multiple users as banned, which means that all their sessions are revoked and they are not allowed to sign in again.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="ban-multiple-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» user_ids|body|[string]|true|Array of user IDs to ban|

## Unban multiple users

<a id="opIdUsersUnban"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/unban \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /users/unban`

Removes the ban mark from multiple users.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» user_ids|body|[string]|true|Array of user IDs to unban|

## Lock a user

<a id="opIdLockUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/lock \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/lock`

Marks the given user as locked, which means they are not allowed to sign in again until the lock expires.
Lock duration can be configured in the instance's restrictions settings.

<h3 id="lock-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user to lock|

## Merge another user into this user

<a id="opIdMergeUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/merge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from_user_id": "string",
    "dry_run": false
  }'
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/merge`

Moves the identifications, connected accounts, passkeys, TOTP, backup codes, organization
memberships, membership requests, suggestions and metadata of the user in `from_user_id` onto the
user in the path, then deletes the `from_user_id` user.
Where both users have a value, the user in the path keeps its own. First and last name, profile
image, `external_id`, and the password are taken from the `from_user_id` user only where the user in
the path has none, so if it has no password, the `from_user_id` user's password signs in to it
afterwards. When both users have the same
identifier, the verified copy is kept. The `from_user_id` user's sessions are revoked.
With `dry_run`, the merge is computed and returned but nothing is changed.

A merge cannot be undone. The response's `deleted_user` is the `from_user_id` user as it was before
the merge, so store it if you may need it. It does not include passwords, TOTP secrets, backup codes,
passkeys or connected-account tokens, which cannot be restored. Use `dry_run` to preview a merge.

The merge sends a `user.merged` webhook alongside `user.updated` and `user.deleted`. Webhooks are not
delivered in order, so `user.updated` (the user now owning the `from_user_id` user's emails) can arrive
before `user.deleted`; handle `user.merged` by moving the `from_user_id` user's data to the user rather
than relying on that order. Moved organization memberships keep their ID, so their
`organizationMembership.updated` webhook carries the same membership ID with a different user.

Some users cannot be merged. The request then fails with a 409 `user_merge_not_allowed` error whose
`meta.reasons` lists every reason that applies:
- `user_banned`, `from_user_banned`: either user is banned.
- `user_directory_managed`, `from_user_directory_managed`: either user is linked to a SCIM directory.
- `from_user_enterprise_account`: the `from_user_id` user has a SAML or enterprise SSO account.
- `from_user_billing_payer`: the `from_user_id` user is a billing payer.
- `from_user_student_pack`: the `from_user_id` user has claimed a student pack.
- `too_many_resources`: the users have too many identifications and organization memberships, requests
  and suggestions combined to merge in one request. This reason is returned on its own.
- `same_user`: `from_user_id` is the user in the path.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from_user_id": "string",
  "dry_run": false
}
```

<h3 id="merge-another-user-into-this-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user that remains after the merge|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» from_user_id|body|string|true|The ID of the user to merge into the user in the path. This user is deleted.|
|» dry_run|body|boolean|false|Return the merged user without changing anything.|

<h3 id="merge-another-user-into-this-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Request was not successful|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid request parameters|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|

<h3 id="merge-another-user-into-this-user-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user|[User](#schemauser)|true|none|none|
|deleted_user|[User](#schemauser)|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Set user profile image

<a id="opIdSetUserProfileImage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/profile_image \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/profile_image`

Update a user's profile image

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
```

<h3 id="set-user-profile-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user to update the profile image for|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|false|none|

## Replace a user's metadata

<a id="opIdReplaceUserMetadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/metadata \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "public_metadata": {},
    "private_metadata": {},
    "unsafe_metadata": {}
  }'
```

`PUT /users/{user_id}/metadata`

Replace a user's metadata attributes with the provided values.

Unlike `PATCH /v1/users/{user_id}/metadata` (merge semantics), this endpoint
replaces the supplied metadata fields entirely — the prior contents of each
supplied field are discarded. Fields omitted from the request body are
left unchanged.

Prefer the `PATCH` endpoint for partial updates. Use `PUT` only when you
explicitly intend to overwrite a metadata field wholesale.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {},
  "unsafe_metadata": {}
}
```

<h3 id="replace-a-users-metadata-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user whose metadata will be replaced|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» public_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the user, that is visible to both your frontend and backend.<br>The existing value will be replaced entirely with the new object.|
|» private_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the user that is only visible to your backend.<br>The existing value will be replaced entirely with the new object.|
|» unsafe_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the user, that can be updated from both the Frontend and Backend APIs.<br>The existing value will be replaced entirely with the new object.<br><br>Note: Since this data can be modified from the frontend, it is not guaranteed to be safe.|

## Merge and update a user's metadata

<a id="opIdUpdateUserMetadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/metadata \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "public_metadata": {},
    "private_metadata": {},
    "unsafe_metadata": {}
  }'
```

`PATCH /users/{user_id}/metadata`

Update a user's metadata attributes by merging existing values with the provided parameters.

This endpoint behaves differently than the *Update a user* endpoint.
Metadata values will not be replaced entirely.
Instead, a deep merge will be performed.
Deep means that any nested JSON objects will be merged as well.

You can remove metadata keys at any level by setting their value to `null`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "public_metadata": {},
  "private_metadata": {},
  "unsafe_metadata": {}
}
```

<h3 id="merge-and-update-a-users-metadata-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user whose metadata will be updated and merged|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» public_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the user, that is visible to both your frontend and backend.<br>The new object will be merged with the existing value.|
|» private_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the user that is only visible to your backend.<br>The new object will be merged with the existing value.|
|» unsafe_metadata|body|object|false|Metadata saved on the user, that can be updated from both the Frontend and Backend APIs.<br>The new object will be merged with the existing value.<br><br>Note: Since this data can be modified from the frontend, it is not guaranteed to be safe.|

## Retrieve a user's billing subscription

<a id="opIdGetUserBillingSubscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/billing/subscription \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/{user_id}/billing/subscription`

Retrieves the billing subscription for the specified user.
This includes subscription details, active plans, billing information, and payment status.
The subscription contains subscription items which represent the individual plans the user is subscribed to.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-users-billing-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user whose subscription to retrieve|

## Adjust a user's credit balance

<a id="opIdAdjustUserBillingCreditBalance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/billing/credits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 0,
    "action": "increase",
    "currency": "string",
    "idempotency_key": "string",
    "note": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/billing/credits`

Increases or decreases the credit balance for the specified user.
Each adjustment is recorded as a ledger entry. The idempotency_key parameter
ensures that duplicate requests are safely handled.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "action": "increase",
  "currency": "string",
  "idempotency_key": "string",
  "note": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="adjust-a-users-credit-balance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user whose credit balance to adjust|
|body|body|[AdjustCreditBalanceRequest](#schemaadjustcreditbalancerequest)|true|Parameters for the credit balance adjustment|
|» amount|body|integer(int64)|true|The credit amount in cents. Must be greater than zero.|
|» action|body|string|true|Whether to increase or decrease the credit balance.|
|» currency|body|string|false|The currency code (e.g. "USD"). Defaults to USD if not provided.|
|» idempotency_key|body|string|true|A unique key to ensure the adjustment is applied only once. Repeated requests with the same key return the original ledger entry.|
|» note|body|string|false|An optional note to attach to the ledger entry.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|increase|
|» action|decrease|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "object": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "payer_id": "string",
  "amount": {
    "amount": 0,
    "amount_formatted": "string",

    "currency_symbol": "string"
  },

}
```

## Retrieve the OAuth access token of a user

<a id="opIdGetOAuthAccessToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/oauth_access_tokens/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/{user_id}/oauth_access_tokens/{provider}`

Fetch the corresponding OAuth access token for a user that has previously authenticated with a particular OAuth provider.
For OAuth 2.0, if the access token has expired and we have a corresponding refresh token, the access token will be refreshed transparently the new one will be returned.

<h3 id="retrieve-the-oauth-access-token-of-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user for which to retrieve the OAuth access token|
|provider|path|string|true|The ID of the OAuth provider (e.g. `oauth_google`)|
|paginated|query|boolean|false|Whether to paginate the results.<br>If true, the results will be paginated.<br>If false, the results will not be paginated.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "object": "oauth_access_token",
    "external_account_id": "string",
    "provider_user_id": "string",
    "token": "string",
    "expires_at": 0,
    "provider": "string",
    "public_metadata": {},
    "label": "string",
    "scopes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "id_token": "string",
    "token_secret": "string"
  }
]
```

```json
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},

}
```

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/{user_id}/organization_invitations`

Retrieve a paginated list of the user's organization invitations

<h3 id="retrieve-all-invitations-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user whose organization invitations we want to retrieve|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter organization invitations based on their status|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|accepted|
|status|revoked|
|status|expired|

## Remove a user's password

<a id="opIdRemoveUserPassword"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/remove_password \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "sign_out_of_other_sessions": false
  }'
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/remove_password`

Removes the password credential from the given user. This is a privileged operation and does not require the user's current password. Password removal is allowed even when the user has no other sign-in method configured.

If the user does not have a password, the user is returned unchanged and no password-deletion or user-update event is emitted. By default, existing sessions remain active. Set `sign_out_of_other_sessions` to `true` to revoke sessions active when the request is processed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sign_out_of_other_sessions": false
}
```

<h3 id="remove-a-users-password-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user whose password to remove|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» sign_out_of_other_sessions|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to revoke all of the user's active sessions after removing the password.|

## Verify the password of a user

<a id="opIdVerifyPassword"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/verify_password \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "password": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/verify_password`

Check that the user's password matches the supplied input.
Useful for custom auth flows and re-verification.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "password": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-the-password-of-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user for whom to verify the password|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» password|body|string|true|The user password to verify|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "verified": true
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-the-password-of-a-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The provided password was correct.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The user does not have a password set.|None|
|404|Not Found|The user does not exist.|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The provided password was incorrect.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Request was not successful|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|

<h3 id="verify-the-password-of-a-user-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|verified|boolean|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Verify a TOTP or backup code for a user

<a id="opIdVerifyTOTP"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/users/string/verify_totp \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "code": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/verify_totp`

Verify that the provided TOTP or backup code is valid for the user.
Verifying a backup code will result it in being consumed (i.e. it will
become invalid).
Useful for custom auth flows and re-verification.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-a-totp-or-backup-code-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user for whom to verify the TOTP|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» code|body|string|true|The TOTP or backup code to verify|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "verified": true,
  "code_type": "totp"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-a-totp-or-backup-code-for-a-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The provided TOTP or backup code was correct.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The user does not have TOTP configured for their account.|None|
|404|Not Found|The user does not exist.|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The provided TOTP or backup code was incorrect.|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Request was not successful|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|

<h3 id="verify-a-totp-or-backup-code-for-a-user-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|verified|boolean|false|none|none|
|code_type|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code_type|totp|
|code_type|backup_code|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-miscellaneous">Miscellaneous</h1>

Various endpoints that do not belong in any particular category.

## Returns the markup for the interstitial page

<a id="opIdGetPublicInterstitial"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/public/interstitial
```

`GET /public/interstitial`

The Clerk interstitial endpoint serves an html page that loads clerk.js in order to check the user's authentication state.
It is used by Clerk SDKs when the user's authentication state cannot be immediately determined.

<h3 id="returns-the-markup-for-the-interstitial-page-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|frontendApi|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Please use `frontend_api` instead|
|frontend_api|query|string|false|The Frontend API key of your instance|
|publishable_key|query|string|false|The publishable key of your instance|
|proxy_url|query|string|false|The proxy URL of your instance|
|domain|query|string|false|The domain of your instance|
|sign_in_url|query|string|false|The sign in URL of your instance|
|use_domain_for_script|query|boolean|false|Whether to use the domain for the script URL|

<h3 id="returns-the-markup-for-the-interstitial-page-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The interstitial page markup|None|
|400|Bad Request|A required query parameter is missing|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|An infinite redirect loop was detected|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-beta-features">Beta Features</h1>

Modify instance settings that are currently in beta.

## Update instance settings

<a id="opIdUpdateInstanceAuthConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/beta_features/instance_settings \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "restricted_to_allowlist": false,
    "from_email_address": "string",
    "progressive_sign_up": true,
    "test_mode": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /beta_features/instance_settings`

Updates the settings of an instance

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "restricted_to_allowlist": false,
  "from_email_address": "string",
  "progressive_sign_up": true,
  "test_mode": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-instance-settings-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» restricted_to_allowlist|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether sign up is restricted to email addresses, phone numbers and usernames that are on the allowlist.|
|» from_email_address|body|string \| null|false|The local part of the email address from which authentication-related emails (e.g. OTP code, magic links) will be sent.<br>Only alphanumeric values are allowed.<br>Note that this value should contain only the local part of the address (e.g. `foo` for `foo@example.com`).|
|» progressive_sign_up|body|boolean \| null|false|Enable the Progressive Sign Up algorithm. This feature is deprecated, please contact support if you need assistance.|
|» test_mode|body|boolean \| null|false|Toggles test mode for this instance, allowing the use of test email addresses and phone numbers.<br>Defaults to true for development instances.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "instance_settings",
  "id": "string",
  "restricted_to_allowlist": true,
  "from_email_address": "string",
  "progressive_sign_up": true,
  "enhanced_email_deliverability": true
}
```

> 402 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-instance-settings-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|InstanceSettings Server API|Inline|
|402|Payment Required|Payment required|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid request parameters|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|

<h3 id="update-instance-settings-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|string|false|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|id|string|false|none|none|
|restricted_to_allowlist|boolean|false|none|none|
|from_email_address|string|false|none|none|
|progressive_sign_up|boolean|false|none|none|

This setting is retired and no longer affects email delivery; all email is sent through the instance's configured email sending domain. <a id="opIdUpdateProductionInstanceDomain"></a>

> Code samples


<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-waitlist-entries">Waitlist Entries</h1>

Manage waitlist entries.

## List all waitlist entries

<a id="opIdListWaitlistEntries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/waitlist_entries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /waitlist_entries`

Retrieve a list of waitlist entries for the instance.
Entries are ordered by creation date in descending order by default.
Supports filtering by email address or status and pagination with limit and offset parameters.

<h3 id="list-all-waitlist-entries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter waitlist entries by `email_address` or `id`|
|status|query|string|false|Filter waitlist entries by their status|
|order_by|query|string|false|Specify the order of results. Supported values are:<br>- `created_at`<br>- `email_address`<br>- `invited_at`<br><br>Use `+` for ascending or `-` for descending order. Defaults to `-created_at`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|invited|
|status|completed|
|status|rejected|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "waitlist_entry",
      "id": "string",
      "email_address": "user@example.com",
      "status": "pending",
      "is_locked": true,
      "created_at": 0,
      "updated_at": 0,
      "invitation": {
        "object": "invitation",
        "id": "string",
        "email_address": "user@example.com",
        "public_metadata": {},
        "revoked": false,
        "status": "pending",
        "url": "string",
        "expires_at": 0,
        "created_at": 0,
        "updated_at": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "total_count": 0
}
```

<h3 id="list-all-waitlist-entries-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|List of waitlist entries|Inline|

<h3 id="list-all-waitlist-entries-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[WaitlistEntry](#schemawaitlistentry)]|true|none|none|
|total_count|integer|true|none|Total number of waitlist entries|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-proxy-checks">Proxy Checks</h1>

Check if a user is using a proxy.

## Verify the proxy configuration for your domain

<a id="opIdVerifyDomainProxy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/proxy_checks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "domain_id": "string",
    "proxy_url": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /proxy_checks`

This endpoint can be used to validate that a proxy-enabled domain is operational.
It tries to verify that the proxy URL provided in the parameters maps to a functional proxy that can reach the Clerk Frontend API.

You can use this endpoint before you set a proxy URL for a domain. This way you can ensure that switching to proxy-based
configuration will not lead to downtime for your instance.

The `proxy_url` parameter allows for testing proxy configurations for domains that don't have a proxy URL yet, or operate on
a different proxy URL than the one provided. It can also be used to re-validate a domain that is already configured to work with a proxy.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "domain_id": "string",
  "proxy_url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-the-proxy-configuration-for-your-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» domain_id|body|string|false|The ID of the domain that will be updated.|
|» proxy_url|body|string|false|The full URL of the proxy which will forward requests to the Clerk Frontend API for this domain. e.g. https://example.com/__clerk|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "proxy_check",
  "id": "string",
  "domain_id": "string",
  "last_run_at": 0,
  "proxy_url": "string",
  "successful": true,
  "created_at": 0,
  "updated_at": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "long_message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "meta": {}
    }
  ],
  "meta": {},
  "clerk_trace_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-the-proxy-configuration-for-your-domain-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Health check information about a domain's proxy configuration validation attempt.|[ProxyCheck](#schemaproxycheck)|
|400|Bad Request|Request was not successful|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid request parameters|[ClerkErrors](#schemaclerkerrors)|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-organization-domains">Organization Domains</h1>

Manage organization domains.

## Get a list of all domains of an organization.

<a id="opIdListOrganizationDomains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/domains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id}/domains`

Get a list of all domains of an organization.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-all-domains-of-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The organization ID.|
|verified|query|string|false|Filter domains by their verification status. `true` or `false`|
|enrollment_mode|query|string|false|Filter domains by their enrollment mode. Accepts `automatic_invitation`, `automatic_suggestion`, `manual_invitation` or `enterprise_sso`.<br>Prefix a value with `-` to exclude it instead (e.g. `-enterprise_sso`). Include and exclude filters can be combined and compose as AND.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "organization_domain",
      "id": "string",
      "organization_id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "enrollment_mode": "manual_invitation",
      "affiliation_email_address": "string",
      "affiliation_verification": {
        "status": "string",
        "strategy": "string",
        "attempts": 0,
```

## Mark an organization domain's ownership as verified

<a id="opIdVerifyOrganizationDomainOwnership"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organizations/string/domains/string/verify_ownership \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id}/domains/{domain_id}/verify_ownership`

Flips the organization domain's ownership state to verified via the
manual override path, bypassing the self-serve TXT DNS challenge. The
domain row records strategy=`manual_override` and an
`organization_domain.ownership_verified` audit event is emitted with the
same strategy.

Idempotent: re-calling on an already-verified domain returns the current
ownership state without re-emitting the audit event.

<h3 id="mark-an-organization-domains-ownership-as-verified-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization to which the domain belongs|
|domain_id|path|string|true|The ID of the domain|

## List all organization domains

<a id="opIdListAllOrganizationDomains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/organization_domains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization_domains`

Retrieves a list of all organization domains within the current instance.
This endpoint can be used to list all domains across all organizations
or filter domains by organization, verification status, enrollment mode, or search query.

The response includes pagination information and details about each domain
including its verification status, enrollment mode, and associated counts.


<h3 id="list-all-organization-domains-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|query|string|false|The ID of the organization to filter domains by|
|verified|query|string|false|Filter by verification status|
|enrollment_mode|query|[string]|false|Filter by enrollment mode. Prefix a value with `-` to exclude it instead<br>(e.g. `-enterprise_sso`). Include and exclude filters can be combined and compose as AND.|
|query|query|string|false|Search domains by name or organization ID.<br>If the query starts with "org_", it will search by exact organization ID match.<br>Otherwise, it performs a case-insensitive partial match on the domain name.<br><br>Note: An empty string or whitespace-only value is not allowed and will result in a validation error.<br>|
|domains|query|[string]|false|Filter by exact domain names. Accepts multiple values (e.g. domains=example.com&domains=test.org).|
|order_by|query|string|false|Allows to return organization domains in a particular order.<br>At the moment, you can order the returned domains by their `name` or `created_at`.<br>In order to specify the direction, you can use the `+/-` symbols prepended to the property to order by.<br>For example, if you want domains to be returned in descending order according to their `created_at` property, you can use `-created_at`.<br>If you don't use `+` or `-`, then `+` is implied.<br>Defaults to `-created_at`.<br>|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|verified|true|
|verified|false|
|enrollment_mode|manual_invitation|
|enrollment_mode|automatic_invitation|
|enrollment_mode|automatic_suggestion|
|enrollment_mode|enterprise_sso|
|enrollment_mode|-manual_invitation|
|enrollment_mode|-automatic_invitation|
|enrollment_mode|-automatic_suggestion|
|enrollment_mode|-enterprise_sso|

> Example responses

## List all subscription items

<a id="opIdGetCommerceSubscriptionItemList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/commerce/subscription_items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /commerce/subscription_items`

Returns a list of all subscription items for the instance. The subscription items are returned sorted by creation date,
with the newest appearing first. This includes subscriptions for both users and organizations. Pagination is supported.

<h3 id="list-all-subscription-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|paginated|query|boolean|false|Whether to paginate the results.<br>If true, the results will be paginated.<br>If false, the results will not be paginated.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Applies a limit to the number of results returned.<br>Can be used for paginating the results together with `offset`.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Skip the first `offset` results when paginating.<br>Needs to be an integer greater or equal to zero.<br>To be used in conjunction with `limit`.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter subscription items by status|
|payer_type|query|string|false|Filter subscription items by payer type|
|plan_id|query|string|false|Filter subscription items by plan ID|
|include_free|query|boolean|false|Whether to include free plan subscription items|
|query|query|string|false|Search query to filter subscription items by email, user first name, user last name, or organization name.<br>Supports partial matching.|
|user_id|query|string|false|Filter subscription items by user ID|
|organization_id|query|string|false|Filter subscription items by organization ID|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|ended|
|status|past_due|
|status|upcoming|
|status|free_trial|
|payer_type|user|
|payer_type|org|

## Cancel a subscription item

<a id="opIdCancelCommerceSubscriptionItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/commerce/subscription_items/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /commerce/subscription_items/{subscription_item_id}`

Cancel a specific subscription item. The subscription item can be canceled immediately or at the end of the current billing period.

<h3 id="cancel-a-subscription-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_item_id|path|string|true|The ID of the subscription item to cancel|
|end_now|query|boolean|false|Whether to cancel the subscription immediately (true) or at the end of the current billing period (false, default)|

<h1 id="clerk-backend-api-billing">Billing</h1>

## Extend free trial for a subscription item

<a id="opIdExtendBillingSubscriptionItemFreeTrial"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/billing/subscription_items/string/extend_free_trial \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "extend_to": "2026-01-08T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /billing/subscription_items/{subscription_item_id}/extend_free_trial`

Extends the free trial period for a specific subscription item to the specified timestamp.
The subscription item must be currently in a free trial period, and the plan must support free trials.
The timestamp must be in the future and not more than 365 days from the end of the current trial period
This operation is idempotent - repeated requests with the same timestamp will not change the trial period.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "extend_to": "2026-01-08T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="extend-free-trial-for-a-subscription-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_item_id|path|string|true|The ID of the subscription item to extend the free trial for|
|body|body|[ExtendFreeTrialRequest](#schemaextendfreetrialrequest)|true|Parameters for extending the free trial|
|» extend_to|body|string(date-time)|true|RFC3339 timestamp to extend the free trial to.<br>Must be in the future and not more than 365 days from now.|

## Create a price transition for a subscription item

<a id="opIdCreateBillingPriceTransition"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/billing/subscription_items/string/price_transition \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from_price_id": "string",
    "to_price_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /billing/subscription_items/{subscription_item_id}/price_transition`

Creates a price transition for the specified subscription item.
This may create an upcoming subscription item or activate immediately depending on plan and payer rules.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from_price_id": "string",
  "to_price_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-price-transition-for-a-subscription-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_item_id|path|string|true|The ID of the subscription item to transition|
|body|body|[PriceTransitionRequest](#schemapricetransitionrequest)|true|Parameters for the price transition|
|» from_price_id|body|string|true|The current price ID of the subscription item.|
|» to_price_id|body|string|true|The target price ID to transition to.|

## Apply a discount to a subscription item

<a id="opIdApplyBillingSubscriptionItemDiscount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/billing/subscription_items/string/discounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "discount_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /billing/subscription_items/{subscription_item_id}/discounts`

Applies an existing discount to a subscription item.
Manual application is an override path: self-serve distribution rules are not enforced.
At most one active discount is allowed per subscription item; applying a different
discount replaces the currently active one. Re-applying the same active discount returns a conflict.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "discount_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="apply-a-discount-to-a-subscription-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_item_id|path|string|true|The ID of the subscription item to apply the discount to|
|body|body|[ApplyCommerceDiscountRequest](#schemaapplycommercediscountrequest)|true|Parameters for applying the discount|
|» discount_id|body|string|true|The ID of the discount to apply to the subscription item.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Remove a discount from a subscription item

<a id="opIdRemoveBillingSubscriptionItemDiscount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/billing/subscription_items/string/discounts/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /billing/subscription_items/{subscription_item_id}/discounts/{discount_id}`

Removes the active discount from a subscription item.
The discount_id must match the subscription item's currently active discount.

<h3 id="remove-a-discount-from-a-subscription-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscription_item_id|path|string|true|The ID of the subscription item to remove the discount from|
|discount_id|path|string|true|The ID of the discount to remove|

## Create an Admin Portal Link Token

<a id="opIdcreateAdminPortalLinkToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/admin_portal_link_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "organization_id": "string",
    "it_contact_id": "string",
    "scopes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "seconds_until_expiration": 3600
  }'
```

## Revoke an Admin Portal Link Token

<a id="opIdrevokeAdminPortalLinkToken"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.clerk.com/v1/admin_portal_link_tokens/string/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
```

<h2 id="tocS_PasswordHasher">PasswordHasher</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapasswordhasher"></a>
<a id="schema_PasswordHasher"></a>
<a id="tocSpasswordhasher"></a>
<a id="tocspasswordhasher"></a>

```json
"string"
```

The hashing algorithm that was used to generate the password digest.

The algorithms we support at the moment are [`bcrypt`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bcrypt), [`bcrypt_sha256_django`](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.0/topics/auth/passwords/), [`md5`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MD5), `pbkdf2_sha1`, `pbkdf2_sha256`, [`pbkdf2_sha256_django`](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.0/topics/auth/passwords/),
`pbkdf2_sha512`, [`phpass`](https://www.openwall.com/phpass/), `md5_phpass`, [`scrypt_firebase`](https://firebaseopensource.com/projects/firebase/scrypt/),
[`scrypt_werkzeug`](https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/en/3.0.x/utils/#werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash), [`sha256`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2),
[`ldap_ssha`](https://www.openldap.org/faq/data/cache/347.html), the [`argon2`](https://argon2.online/) variants: `argon2i` and `argon2id`, `sha512_symfony`, the SHA-512 variant of the [Symfony](https://symfony.com/doc/current/security/passwords.html) legacy hasher,
and `pbkdf2_sha512_hex`, a variant of `pbkdf2_sha512` that accepts hex-encoded salt and hash.

Each of the supported hashers expects the incoming digest to be in a particular format. See the [Clerk docs](https://clerk.com/docs/references/backend/user/create-user) for more information.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the subscription item.|
|instance_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the Clerk instance.|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the subscription item.|
|credit|object \| null|false|none|Credit information (only available in PaymentAttempt events).|
|plan_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the associated plan.|
|price_id|string|false|none|Unique identifier for the associated price|
|plan|object \| null|true|none|The associated commerce plan.|
|plan_period|string|true|none|The billing period for this subscription.|
|payment_source_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the payment source.|
|payment_source|object \| null|false|none|The payment source associated with this subscription.|
|lifetime_paid|object \| null|false|none|Total amount paid over the lifetime of this subscription.|
|amount|object \| null|false|none|Current amount for this subscription.|
|next_invoice|object \| null|false|none|Information about the next invoice.|
|next_payment|object \| null|false|none|Information about the next payment.|
|payer_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the payer.|
|payer|object \| null|false|none|The payer associated with this subscription.|
|is_free_trial|boolean|true|none|Whether this subscription is currently on a free trial.|
|period_start|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) when the current period started.|
|period_end|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) when the current period ends.|
|proration_date|string|true|none|Date used for proration calculations.|
|canceled_at|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) when the subscription was canceled.|
|past_due_at|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) when the subscription became past due.|
|ended_at|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) when the subscription ended.|
|created_at|integer(int64)|true|none|Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) when the subscription was created.|
|updated_at|integer(int64)|true|none|Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) when the subscription was last updated.|

```json
    "string"
  ],
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|dynamic_oauth_client_registration|boolean|true|none|Whether dynamic OAuth client registration is enabled for the instance (RFC 7591).|
|dynamic_client_allowed_scopes|[string]|false|none|Administrator-selected scope ceiling for dynamically registered and automatically admitted CIMD clients. Null preserves registered client limits; defaults must be a subset. Fresh user consent is required for expansion.|
|default_scopes|[string]|true|none|Default scopes assigned when a dynamically registered or first-contact CIMD client omits `scope`. Contains built-in keys and custom catalog keys. Null means Clerk-provided defaults. `advertised` does not affect eligibility. An empty input array is stored and returned as null.<br>|
|oauth_jwt_access_tokens|boolean|true|none|Whether OAuth JWT access tokens are enabled for the instance (disabled indicates opaque access tokens).|
|aud_claim_enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether OAuth access tokens can include an aud claim derived from the RFC 8707 resource parameter.|
|aud_claim_refresh_backfill_enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether refresh grants without a resource can adopt the requested resource when audience claims are enabled.|
|pkce_required|boolean|true|none|Whether all new OAuth authorization-code requests must use PKCE with the S256 challenge method.|
|client_id_metadata_documents_advertised|boolean|true|none|Whether the instance advertises support for Client ID Metadata Documents in its OAuth authorization server metadata.|
|client_id_metadata_documents_only_allow_pre_registered_clients|boolean|true|none|When true, new unknown CIMD clients are rejected. Previously auto-connected and pre-registered clients remain admitted; deleting a client makes it unknown again.|
|client_id_metadata_documents_block_implicitly_allowed_clients|boolean|true|none|When true, recorded implicitly allowed CIMD clients are rejected on future client lookups. Explicitly allowed clients remain accepted. This does not revoke previously issued access tokens.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|oauth_application_settings|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the price.|
|plan_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the associated plan.|
|instance_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the instance.|
|currency|string|true|none|The currency code (e.g., "USD").|
|currency_symbol|string|true|none|The currency symbol (e.g., "$").|
|amount|integer(int64)|true|none|The amount in cents for the price.|
|annual_monthly_amount|integer(int64)|true|none|The monthly amount in cents when billed annually.|
|fee|object \| null|true|none|none|
|annual_monthly_fee|object \| null|true|none|none|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the price.|
|is_default|boolean|true|none|Whether this price is the default price for its plan.|
|created_at|integer(int64)|true|none|Unix timestamp (milliseconds) of creation.|
|supported_billing_periods|string|true|none|Which billing periods this price supports.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|commerce_price|
|supported_billing_periods|month|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|string|true|none|String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value.|
|id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the discount redemption.|
|subscription_item_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the subscription item the discount was applied to.|
|discount_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the discount that was applied.|
|name|string|false|none|The display name of the discount.|
|source|string|true|none|How the discount was applied to the subscription item.|
|promo_code|string|false|none|The promo code used to redeem the discount, when applicable.|
|effect|string|false|none|The snapshotted discount effect.|
|percent_off|number(double) \| null|false|none|Percent off when the effect is percentage.|
|amount_off|object \| null|false|none|Fixed amount off when the effect is fixed_amount.|
|amount|object \| null|false|none|How much this discount takes off the subscription item's next renewal charge.<br>Present for either effect when next-payment data is available.|
|cycles_remaining|integer(int32) \| null|true|none|Remaining billing cycles the discount applies to. Null means the discount lasts forever.|
|cycles_applied|integer(int32)|true|none|Number of billing cycles the discount has already been applied to.|
|status|string|false|none|Current status of the discount redemption.|
|redeemed_at|integer(int64)|true|none|Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) when the discount was redeemed.|
|redeemed_by|string \| null|true|none|Identifier of the actor that redeemed the discount, when available.|

|mappings|object \| null|false|none|Role key mappings from source to destination roles|
